articleTitle: Low Cost GNSS Receiver RTK Performance in Forest Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Requirement of accuracy and reliability of position solution obtained from satellite-Based navigation system provided by the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) depends on the application. In some cases, meter level precision is required while cm or mm level accuracy is required for other precision applications. Surveying is one of the important applications of GNSS. Surveying of forest is a challenge for survey engineers in determining accurate position, because satellite signals frequently fade by stems and leaves of the tress. Consequently, the observables become noisy that affects quality of position solution. Real Time Kinematic (RTK) is a popular GNSS positioning method used in case of various precision applications. High cost receivers may provide better RTK solution those are not affordable for many surveyors. Low cost, single frequency, multi-GNSS enabled receiver are available in market those can provide raw data and can be used for RTK. In this paper an effort is presented to assess the precision and reliability of position solution obtained from the low-cost receivers within Indian forest environments. In the first case study over a short baseline, position solution precision provided by a low-cost Rover operating in forest is studied, and meter level of precision is achieved in GPS+GLONASS+Galileo mode. In second case study for long baseline RTK operation, reliable solution is obtained in GPS+Galileo+QZSS mode from a low-cost Rover operating within forest environment. So, reliable or precise position solution can be achieved using low cost receivers and suitable multi-GNSS combination under forest canopy.

articleTitle: A Pentagon-Shaped Microstrip Patch Antenna with Slotted Ground Plane for RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a single band antenna operating at 2.45 GHz has been introduced for RF energy harvesting applications. The antenna structure consists of a pentagonal shaped radiating patch and is energized by microstrip feeding technique. A rectangular-shaped slot is embedded in the ground plane to improve the impedance matching, gain characteristics at the desired frequency. An operating bandwidth of 240 MHz (2.33-2.57 GHz) centred at 2.45 GHz is obtained with the proposed configuration. The harvesting antenna is designed using low-cost FR4 substrate of thickness 1.6 mm and has an overall dimension of 100×100×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The designed antenna provides stable Omni-directional radiation characteristics with a maximum gain of 8.02 dBi.

articleTitle: CRLH Transmission Line Based Compact Metamaterial Inspired Antenna for Wi-MAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a new and compact open ended metamaterial (MTM) antenna based on composite right/left handed (CRLH) transmission line is presented. Compactness is achieved due to zeroth order resonance (ZOR) property of MTM. The proposed antenna has overall electrical size of 0.22λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.22λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.014λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is wavelength calculated at 2.64 GHz and physical size of 25 × 25 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna covers frequencies from 2.55-2.75 GHZ which is equivalent to 7.6 % fractional bandwidth (-10 dB). The main advantage of intended antenna is its high gain of 3.17 dBi at ZOR frequency 2.64 GHz with radiation efficiency 98.63%. A via less single layer coplanar waveguide (CPW) feeding technique gives the advantage of easy fabrication. Another advantage of this antenna is its exceptional low cross polarization level which is found as -52.9 dB for both the planes. Acceptable impedance matching, high gain, and satisfactory radiation pattern are obtained throughout the operation band, it makes antenna good candidate for working efficiently in 2.5 GHz Wi-MAX applications.

articleTitle: A Compact, T-Slotted Wide Band Microstrip Antenna with Defected Ground Structure for Future 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this article, a compact wide-band microstrip patch Antenna with defected ground square structure is presented. The article presents the application for 5th generation wireless communication. The antenna is designed over a ground plane, having a minimal size of 0.308λo × 0.308λo × 0.009λo with design centre frequency 22 GHz. In order to enhance the antenna bandwidth, a T-shaped slotted Patch and rectangular notch has been introduced. The antenna is covering a wideband of frequency range 23.60 GHz to 44.20 GHz, with a gain of 4.198 dB at 27.30 GHz and 4.703dB at 39.90 GHz centre frequency. The proposed antenna is compact as well as suited for higher band of 5G communications. In addition, the designed antenna exhibits omni-directional radiation pattern which is required for 5G applications.

articleTitle: V2X Communication Test Bed for Smart Electrical Vehicle with 5G IOV Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In an attempt to make road vehicles smarter, authors have engaged in the design and development of CV2X (Cellular Vehicle to Anything) communication system in its physical layer. They have imparted continuous efforts in several steps in developing test bed. 5G IoV waveform is chosen for CV2X communication where the broadband 5G waveform will provide infotainment to the passenger and narrowband IoV waveform will provide vehicular communication and enable the automatic control of vehicles. Multi-Standard Radio (MSR) is used to realize the waveform. At the initial stage, test bed design for 5G IoV Multiservice Transmitter is modeled using Systemvue EDA (Electronic Design Automation) software. Then the model has been downloaded to a Vector Signal Generator (VSG) which will act as a 5G IoV transmitter. 5G IoV transmitter design is validated by receiving the transmitted signal over the air mode using one TV receiver and FM receiver. A field trial is initiated by putting the said transmitter in one vehicle and receiver in another vehicle.

articleTitle: Compact Superwideband Terahertz Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip line fed ring shaped terahertz monopole antenna for superwideband applications. It comprises a tetradecagonal ring shaped monopole and modified ground plane. It has an operating bandwidth of 0.45-18.08 THz for VSWR ≤ 2 with an overall volume of 800µm×570µm×81.29µm. It has stable radiation patterns and a peak gain of 15.405 dB. The proposed antenna has merits of superwide bandwidth and miniaturized dimensions over previously reported structures.

articleTitle: Meander Line and Loop Resonator Loaded Dual Band Electrically Small Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of dual band electrically small antenna loaded with meander line and loop resonator. The proposed electrically small antenna (ESA) is designed on the FR-4 substrate with modified ground plane. The radiating element of the proposed antenna consists of metallic strip loaded with thin inductive meander line and a resonant triangular loop. The presented configuration gives dual band response at 1.81 GHz and 2.56 GHz. The higher resonance frequency is controlled by tuning the effective length of metallic strip. The lower frequency response i.e. 1.81 GHz is achieved by using the combination of the shunt inductive meander lines topped with a triangular loop resonator. The surface area of the presented antenna is 40 mm× 15 mm. The designed antenna exhibits fractional bandwidth of 3.8% and 21% for 1.81 GHz, and 2.56 GHz respectively. The measured and simulated results are in near agreement proving the effectivity of the resonator.

articleTitle: Scalp – Implantable Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents implantable antenna systems which are miniaturized and it is proposed for biomedical applications, particularly for scalp administration. The advanced prototypes reveal the broad band features on the industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) bands. Every structure is concatenated with the microelectronic constituents and a battery. The methodology and the operation are discussed briefly in this paper. The results of scalp implantable antenna produces a band from 0.9GHz to 0.92GHz. The measurements are fulfilled in an isotonic solution of sodium chloride for validation. The antenna proposes a fine accordance between the simulated and firmed results and to examine the range of the data transmission, a link budget is calculated.

articleTitle: Study of Temperature Sensitivity on Linearity Figures of Merit of Ge/Si Hetero-Junction Gate-Drain Underlapped Vertical Tunnel FET with heterogeneous gate dielectric structure for Improving Device Reliability
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this work, temperature sensitivity on linearity figures of merit for a heterogeneous gate dielectric based Ge/Si heterojunction vertical tunnel field effect transistor (TFET) with gate-drain underlap structure has been reported. A source pocket is considered in between source and channel for both the structure to enhance the performance of the device. In the same time, consideration of different device engineered architectures which includes gate-drain underlap and heterogeneous gate dielectric (material having higher dielectric constant is placed nearer to the source end) are made to improve sub-threshold performance of the proposed device. The DC performances in terms of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> and sub-threshold swing are investigated for the proposed device. In addition to this, operating temperature effect on device transfer and output characteristics are thoroughly investigated by varing the temperature from 250 K to 450 K. Subsequently, effect of variation in operating temperature on the linearity figures of merit (FOMs) such as higher order transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m2</inf>,g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m3</inf>), VIP2,VIP3,IIP3, and IDM3 are analyzed for different temperature ranging from 250 K to 450 K. The commercially available SILVACO ATLAS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> TCAD simulation tool has been used to analyze the performance of the proposed device.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Pentagonal Superwideband Fractal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A new compact circle circumscribed pentagonal fractal antenna for superwideband applications is presented in this paper. It comprises third iterative circle circumscribed pentagonal radiator, coplanar waveguide feeding and asymmetrical ground planes. The simulated bandwidth is 3.6-36.2 GHz (i.e 32.6 GHz) and 3.5-37 GHz (33.5GHz) for Ansoft HFSS and CST MWS respectively. The overall dimensions of proposed antenna are 28x27x1.6 mm3. It has peak gain of 8.05 dBi. The proposed antenna has advantages of miniaturized size and wider bandwidth over previously reported structures.

articleTitle: Gain Improvement of Ultra-Wideband antenna using compact Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A printed ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna of dimension 36×24 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is combined to a very compact single layered UWB FSS structure which has unit cell size of 11×11 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> only. The ‘antenna-FSS’ structure offers an impedance bandwidth from 2.94 to 15.26 GHz (135%) with an average gain improvement of 3 to 4 dBi. The maximum gain escalation of about 5.2 dBi is realized at 8.9 GHz. Also flat group delay response and linear transfer function profiles are realized. The performance of antenna-FSS combined structure is compared to the recently reported antenna-FSS structures to investigate the improvement of proposed design.

articleTitle: A Cavity-Backed Circular SIW Antenna for X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A cavity-backed circular substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is designed to radiate at 10 GHz. It has high power handling capacity along with unidirectional high broadside peak gain of 7.3 dBi due to its cavity-backed structure. By varying the radius of the annular slot, the antenna can be operated throughout the X-band and hence, frequency tunability is achieved with its simple structure. The antenna exhibits a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 4.1% at its resonant frequency and a front-toback ratio of 15 dB. The proposed antenna is a suitable candidate for X-band high gain unidirectional narrowband applications.

articleTitle: Dual Band Energy Harvester Based on Metasurface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A dual band energy harvesting scheme using nested ELC resonator based metasurface is presented in this paper. The metasurface acts as an electromagnetic energy absorber at two different frequencies and the absorbed energy is channeled to a resistor which can act as effective load/rectifier circuit in practical scenario. Simulation results shows more than 90% absorption by the unit cell and 80% power dissipation across the resistor at both the frequencies. Proposed metasurface based energy harvester circuit is designed and simulated in a FEM based commercial electromagnetic solver. Fabrication of the prototype is currently under progress. Measured results will be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Dual-band Bandpass filter using SIW cavity with E-shaped DGS
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of broadly separated second-order dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity with E-shaped defected ground structure (DGS). The lower frequency passband is generated by back to back coupled DGSs. The back to back coupled E-shaped DGS gives two transmission zeros (TZs) which increase roll-off characteristics of first passband and increase attenuation between the passbands. Also, the SIW cavity with slot perturbation has been used to shift down TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf> mode and give a passband along with TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> mode at high frequency. The proposed filter is synthesized using RT/duroid 5880 substrate of thickness 0.51 mm. The center frequencies are 5.37 GHz and 10.38 GHz and the ratio of center frequencies is 1.93.

articleTitle: Analysis of some important parameters of Si-Ge-Sn RCE-HPT exploiting QCSE and FKE
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The performance of a resonant cavity enhanced Heterobipolar Phototransistor with Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.992</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.008</inf>/Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.61</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.09</inf> Quantum Well under Quantum Confined Stark Effect has been presented here. Further the Quantum Wells are replaced by GeSn bulk absorption region to estimate the influence of Franz Keldysh Effect..

articleTitle: On the Design of Four-Element Pattern Diversity MIMO Antennas for Mutual Coupling Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: We revisit the design procedure of printed four element pattern diversity antennas, starting from the concept of printed dipoles on dielectric substrates arranged in a rotationally symmetric configuration. We systematically modify this basic dipole-based configuration to realize electrical miniaturization, wideband performance and sectorial beam-forming. Especially, we show that by utilizing stub-like structures analogous to neutralization lines, the port-to-port mutual coupling can be significantly reduced in the working band, without gain-reduction or pattern distortion.

articleTitle: A Cross-Dipole Shaped Patch-Slot-Patch Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A patch-slot-patch frequency selective surface (FSS) exhibiting bandpass response is proposed in this paper. The FSS unit cell is composed of two cross-dipole shaped patches and a cross-dipole shaped slot in between. The proposed FSS exhibits bandpass response with two closely spaced transmission poles around 3 GHz and 3.5 GHz. A 3-dB transmission bandwidth of upto 20% is achieved for the FSS. The proposed design has a thickness on the order of 0.032 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> . The paper presents with parametric studies how the poles can be tuned individually. The transmission phase of the FSS varies linearly towards zero with frequency that makes the FSS useful in designing Filter-Antenna when placed as a superstrate above a broadside radiator.

articleTitle: Design of Front-End Modules for MMwave 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Beam steering antenna and wideband up/down converters are essential building blocks for the deployment of 5G communication at mmwave bands. In India, a band around 26GHz is likely to be chosen for the purpose. Key design elements of these building blocks are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Resonance SIW Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dual resonance cavity-backed slot antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide for the fifth-generation (5G) applications are designed and simulated to cover both Europe (24.25 – 27.5 GHz ) and USA region (27.5 – 28.35 GHz). With the proper positioning of multi-resonant slots on the bottom metal cladding of the SIW cavity, the hybrid modes are generated in the frequency band of interest. These modifications can be adjusted by varying the parameters of the slots, which result in the merging of different resonance frequencies. The results show that the bandwidth of 4.6 GHz (17.24%) ranging from 24.2 GHz – 28.8 GHz, a gain of 7.8 dBi and 9.2 dBi over the bandwidth, and cross-polarization level less than −35 dB have been achieved. The proposed antenna is compared in terms of antenna performances including reflection coefficient, bandwidth, gain, optimized parameter values, and radiation pattern with previously reported work in the literature. The overall volume occupied by the proposed design including feedline is 18 mm x 12 mm x 0.508 mm.

articleTitle: Effect of Vibration on the Cathode Lead of Electron Gun Assembly of the Travelling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Device Technology Group, Microwave Devises Area, CSIR-Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute, Pilani-333031, Rajasthan, India In the electron gun assembly cathode is the main source of electron beam. Cathode lead connected to the cathode assembly is the smallest and flexible part of whole Travelling Wave Tube (TWT). TWT has to face several mechanical vibration loads during satellite launching condition and upper stage separation. Therefore, it is important to study the effect of vibration on electron gun assembly before integrating it with the other TWT components. The electron gun assembly is the lightest part of TWT but performance and efficiency of the TWT are highly depends on it. In these paper authors have presented the study of electron gun assembly under the sine vibration, random vibration and static acceleration vibration case using ANSYS tool. There is a very good factor of safety over allowable strength of the cathode lead part of electron gun assembly.

articleTitle: An Approach To Estimate Wall Parameters Using Genetic Algorithm And Time-domain Reflection Method For Through-Wall Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Through wall imaging system is emerging technology to sense objects behind the wall. In these systems, the wall parameter is needed to be estimated a priori to form through the wall radar images. Incorrect estimation of these parameters causes blurriness in the radar image and a shift in the position of the object from its actual position. Therefore, in the present paper, a novel wall parameter estimation method from the time domain data has presented that estimate the parameters of wall such as its relative permitivity and thickness by solving a nonlinear optimization problem based on genetic algorithm. From the experiment result, the estimated wall parameter have found close to the actual value.

articleTitle: A Low-cost Approach towards Ionospheric Probing Using Compact GNSS Receivers
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Besides core services like Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT), Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is used for atmospheric and ionosphere probing since the deployment of the systems. Costly and high data rate geodetic receivers are usually used for such research. These receivers may not be affordable for many users and cost reduction of probing systems may be useful for ongoing research. Low cost, compact, multi-frequency and multiple constellation enabled GNSS modules are recently being increasingly available in market those may be used for atmospheric or ionospheric research. In this manuscript, study results on suitability of such compact, cost-efficient GNSS modules for GNSS-based ionospheric research is presented. Low-cost single board computers (Raspberry Pi, RPi) interfaced with the module may be used for data recording. Approximate cost for such complete prototype unit would be around USD 360 (around INR 26,000) Signal strengths of GNSS satellites in terms of C/NO values may be extracted from the recorded NMEA data sentences and related atmospheric parameters can be derived from the C/NO values. This low cost, compact setup may be deployed at a fixed location or multiple such units may be deployed over a distributed geographical region for realtime, networked monitoring purpose. A comparative study on signal strength obtained from standard survey grade GNSS receivers and such low-cost receivers is made. For the module used in this effort, 6dB-Hz difference is witnessed between the values, but both the types show similar signature of signal strength variation. A properly calibrated system may be useful for designing cost- effective, GNSS-based ionospheric research.

articleTitle: Travelling-Wave Tubes for Space Application: Present and Future
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Traveling wave tube amplifiers (TWTAs) and solid-state power amplifiers (SSPAs) are the two main RF amplifiers for onboard communications satellites. In fact, TWTAs are the first successful RF power amplifier technology for communication systems since the birth of space age and covers ~ 60% global market among vacuum tubes for various applications. Both uplinked and downlink signals experience substantial losses and hence must be suitably amplified. However, demand for high power, high frequency, wideband, high efficiency and with the advancements technology such as linearization, miniaturization, weight reduction, etc, makes TWTAs superior compare to SSPAs and also in the family of vacuum microwave devices and resulting TWTAs as the best choice and no other amplifiers can give similar performance. With advancement of state-of-the-art TWTs for space communication, for instance, wideband, high power, gain efficiency, reliability, light weight etc make realization of space TWT more and more complex and challenging. However, many of the older version of TWTs have been replaced by its counterpart, SSPA, in L, S, C and X bands where both power and bandwidth requirements were limited. In present generation of TWTs, C, X, Ku and Ka band TWTs are being used with wideband width and much higher performances where SSPAs cannot rival. In addition to that, with the agility of wideband, high frequency, much higher performance in a single device for next generation realization of space TWTs in above band including W band and so on becoming a challenge to designers. This paper, presents the state-of-the-art space TWTs for present and future communication satellites.

articleTitle: Asymmetric transmission and cross polarization conversion of linearly polarized wave through metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this article, a bi-layer chiral metasurface constituting of two complementary twisted pairs of split ring resonators (SRRs) having inclined metal patch are printed on both faces of a dielectric slab. Through this unique geometry, quality transmission with excellent wideband polarization conversion ratio, more than 80% between 9.60 GHz and 10.87 GHz have been achieved. The calculated efficiency of this particular transmitter type cross polarizer is 85.58% at 10.25 GHz, where the co-polarized reflection coefficient becomes minimum while the cross-polarization reflection coefficient becomes enhanced. A strong asymmetric transmission has been experienced under the exposure of the linearly polarized electromagnetic wave (EM) for both forward and backward propagation.

articleTitle: Dual band printed wide-slot antenna for Wi-Fi and WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A simply designed dual band printed planar antenna with two opposite directional spline shaped patch and a wide slot at the bottom of substrate, opposite to the co-planar feed is proposed in this article. The antenna of dimension 100×100×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, can covers the 2.4 GHz to 2.61 GHz band for Wi-Fi application and 4.95-5.3 GHz band to cover the lower WLAN. Moreover the similar wide-slot antenna with single spline shaped patch is also proposed that can cover the 5 GHz ISM band. The antennas also provide desired radiation patterns in the operational band with maximum gain value of 6 dBi and radiation efficiency of more than 70%.

articleTitle: Level Estimation with Radar Level Probe using Multipath Reduction Technique
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In Industries there is presence of huge tanks working at extreme conditions of temperature and pressure. Accurate measurement of level is important in these applications. Radar based level probes are advantageous since they are non-contact. Many alternatives in level measurement work in contact with the liquid. These do not work in long term since reactions happen if the liquid is corrosive and the instrument get corroded. When using radar for level measurement, the tank being metallic enclosure lead to presence of multipath signals in the spectrum. This makes target detection difficult. Attenuation of the multipath signals become important while level measurement.In this paper, level measurement in tank filled with water using X band FMCW radar in multipath scenario is shown. Empty tank spectrum subtraction from the measured spectrum is done along with bin limiting to improve target detection. These results in the reduction of multipath signals from the measured spectrum and improve the SNR of the signals.

articleTitle: Multi-time Snapshot based Off-Grid DOA Estimation of Sparse Array Antennas using MFOCUSS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: An off the grid direction-of-arrival estimation of the signals originating from quasi static targets is suggested in this paper using compressive sensing based sparse reconstruction of multiple time snapshot MFOCUSS algorithm. Simulation outcomes show that multi-snapshot restoration of the target location gives more accurate results in terms of root-mean-square error with respect to single snapshot instance.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact SIW Diplexer with Square Cavities for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of compact substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) diplexer with square cavities for C-band applications is presented. This diplexer is working on evanescent-mode propagation and operating below the cut-off frequency of the cavity. First, the filtering response of triangular-slot loaded on one square cavity surface is investigated. This response of the cavity is then applied on two cascaded filters to obtain the diplexer characteristics. To validate the concept, a narrow band filter and diplexer are designed and simulated. The insertion losses at lower and upper passbands centered at 6.16 GHz and 7.72 GHz are obtained as 0.83 dB and 0.77 dB, respectively. The proposed diplexer provides a fractional bandwidth more than 5.1% at each passband with high isolation better than 22 dB. These features show that the proposed diplexer is a suitable candidate for C-band application.

articleTitle: Minkowski Fractal Parasitic Slot Antenna for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A compact printed parasitic slot antenna integrated with Minkowski fractal patch for wideband applications is proposed in this paper. The design is mounted on FR-4 substrate with height h = 1.6 mm and a simple 500Ω microstrip line feed is used to excite the rotated slot of the antenna. The Minkowski fractal patch reduces the overall radiator size and increases the bandwidth compared to the conventional square patch. Four stubs introduced in the design further enhance the bandwidth of the antenna as well as the omnidirectional radiation pattern. The simulation results shows that this design exhibits a bandwidth improvement by 88.87% as compared to the antenna without the stub. Further, the triple notched bands of proposed antenna can accommodate the channel 3 of IEEE 802.11g (2.41 -2.43 GHz), the lower band of 5G technology at 2.5 GHz and can be used at X-band .

articleTitle: A Novel Configuration of Stepped Rectangular Printed Monopole Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this work, a novel configuration of printed monopole antenna for use in ultra-wideband (UWB) systems is presented. The proposed antenna features a compact microstrip fed stepped rectangular printed monopole accompanied by a partial ground plane. The antenna structure is designed on the FR4 substrate having an overall dimension of 32×25×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The designed antenna demonstrates an operating bandwidth of 8.3 GHz ranging from 2.9-11.2 GHz. A maximum gain of 3.5 dBi is also achieved. For design and simulation purpose, ANSYS HFSS tool is used. The suggested design is compact in size and suitable for operating in the entire UWB frequency band of 3.1-10.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Lateral HfO2/SiO2 Gate Stacked TFET on SELBOX Substrate for Low Power and High-Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this work, we have designed a novel device which is working on the principle of band to band tunneling, called as lateral HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate stacked TFET on SELBOX substrate (LGS-STFET). The gap created near the source region to form a SEL-BOX structure is responsible for reducing the off-state current. DC and RF analysis have been investigated in this work for our proposed device along with conventional SEL-BOX TFET (C-STFET). From DC analysis, it is observed that sub-threshold swing (SS) of the proposed device is very low (22.5 mV/dec) compared to conventional SELBOX TFET (C-STFET). In the RF analysis, maximum transit frequency of the proposed device (LGS-STFET) is found to be 60 GHz as compared to conventional SELBOX TFET (2.26 GHz). The DC/RF parameters like transfer characteristics, transconductance, gate to drain capacitance, transit frequency, transit delay, and gain-bandwidth product (GBP) of the proposed TFET have been compared with C-STFET in this manuscript. All the DC and RF parameters analysis have done through simulation by using ATLAS TCAD tool.

articleTitle: NRD to Microstrip Transition Using PLA Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this we designed microstrip to NRD(Non-Radiative Dielectric) transition is designed using 3d printing technology. In the proposed structure Polylactic Acid (PLA) used in 3D printing as a dielectric medium in (NRD). NRD to microstrip transition is designed, simulated and physically realized around 47 GHz. Here simulation has been carried out by using HFSS 17. The advantage and shortcomings of PLA made using additive printing technology like 3D printing is discussed in detail. In the result section, we observed the value of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> and compare the simulated and fabricated results.

articleTitle: Now casting of Orographic Rain Rate Using ARIMA and ANN Model
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Frequent occurrence of Orographic precipitation in hills during most of the time of a year causes severe landslide which has adverse effect on the habitat around it. Therefore now casting of rainfall in terms of rain rate sufficient time ahead is very urgent need to save society from severe disaster. Therefore using statistical method like Auto regressive integrated moving average model (ARIMA) or using artificial neural network (ANN), now casting of rain rate had been done in the literature and the two methods are compared in this work in terms of error performance. The retrieval error indicates the performance of the ANN model is best, however both the method shows acceptable prediction.

articleTitle: Improved Design of Ka-band Waveguide to Coaxial Right Angle Microwave Transition
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The Ka-band (26.5-40 GHz) standard waveguide (WR28) to 50Ω Coaxial (2.92mm Female) microwave transition has been designed indigenously. This is a short-ended ridged waveguide design with disc-loaded coaxial probe [1] based on the principles of field matching and impedance matching. It’s achieved through ridged waveguide, customized coaxial probe and back-short distance [2]-[3]. The compact single piece transition results in the light weight, ease in integration and improved RF leakage of < -88dBm (measured). The full two-port adapter-removal (AR) technique [4]-[5] is used for measuring Scattering parameters on VNA. The measured VSWR and insertion loss are achieved < 1.145 and better than 0.38dB respectively. This reflects significant improvement in comparison with the standard transition (as part of the VNA calibration kit) with VSWR <1.196 and insertion loss better than 0.47dB.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Metallic Post Integrated Patch Antenna for Road Transport and Traffic Telematics Application at 5.8 GHz DSRC Band
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A left hand circularly polarized (LHCP) circular microstrip patch antenna (CMSA), operating at 5.8 GHz dedicated short range communication (DSRC) band using metallic posts (MPs) is explored in this paper for road transport and traffic telematics (RTTT) application. Optimal tuning of the distance between each pair of MPs a 176◦ wide axial ratio (AR) beamwidth for on-board unit (OBU) antenna is achieved. The OBU antenna offers a 18.5 dB cross-polarization isolation well-above the European standard (CEN-EN12253) for RTTT application. Analysis of the OBU integrated on a car model is also done to evaluate the effect of a large electromagnetic object on the antenna performance. The OBU antenna integrated on a vehicle offers a considerably high gain of 10.4 dBic with the 3 dB AR beamwidth of 298◦ and 236◦ in E-plane and H-plane, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency distribution of aerosol optical depth over Varanasi during 2011
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This work is based on the distribution of aerosol optical depth (AOD) over Varanasi site (25.27<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>N, 82.99<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>E). Ground based measurement is taken from MICROTOPSII sunphotometer and satellite based image data is taken from Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS). AOD is found to be vary mostly between 0.4 to 1.0 and Angstrom Exponent showing variation between 0.5 – 0.7 and 0.9 – 1.3, which shows mixture of course mode as well as fine mode aerosol particles over Varanasi.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Yagi Slot Antenna using AMC Substrate
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified Yagi slot antenna with triple bands and enhanced gain for wearable applications. The proposed design consists of a coplanar fed slot microstrip Yagi antenna backed by an AMC substrate and a ground plane which shows an effective triple operational bandwidth. The AMC has been designed to operate at 7.9 GHz and the performance comparisons have been carried out with and without using AMC substrate. The AMC layer comprises 5×7-unit cell array to form the back reflector for Yagi antenna. The proposed antenna exhibits 4.2%, 12% and 1.6% impedance bandwidths corresponding to 2.84 GHz, 7.64 GHz and 9.66 GHz respectively. The overall gain enhancement of about 8 dBi has been achieved and shows end fire characteristics. The proposed antenna with high gain is a potential candidate for RFID, defense and several medical applications.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Comparison of Printed Monopole Antennas with Elliptical Radiator for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper introduces two simple designs of printed monopole antennas with elliptical radiator, based on perturbed ground planes, for use in UWB systems. These two designs are implemented on 0.8 mm thick FR4 substrate. By feeding the radiating element along the major and minor axis, respectively, with truncated ground plane, two different configurations are achieved that realizes wider impedance bandwidth satisfying the UWB specifications. The first designed antenna exhibits an operating bandwidth from 3.21 GHz-12.38 GHz, whereas for the case of second design, the bandwidth is enhanced to a wider frequency range varying from 1.6-12.40 GHz. Omni-directional radiation patterns, along with appreciable gain characteristics for both antenna configurations are obtained in this paper.

articleTitle: Comparison of Time & Frequency Sources using NavIC Signals
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) formerly known as Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) provides geo-spatial positioning with regional coverage over Indian landmass extended upto 1500 km. In general, NavIC have three main segments, namely the space segment, the ground segment and the user segment. Precise Timing Facility (PTF) is an important element of the NavIC ground segment responsible for generating and disseminating NavIC System Time. The system time is generated using an ensemble of highly stable atomic clocks and is continuously steered towards Co-ordinated Universal Time (UTC). Two timing laboratories have been established as a part of NavIC Ground segment with one as a primary and another as a backup facility. It therefore necessitates to continuous compare the time offsets between the system time generated at the two remotely located timing facilities in order to have smooth transition from one site to another for navigation operation. The offset between the two remotely located timescales can be done using multiple time transfer techniques. This paper provides the first results for the offsets between two time and frequency sources using NavIC Common view time transfer. This provides an alternate and independent way to compare the remotely located time and frequency sources with similar accuracy. The results obtained using NavIC Common View Time Transfer are validated against other techniques.

articleTitle: Y-Shaped Antenna for 5G Enabled Gadgets and its MIMO for Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper a very small Y-shaped micro strip antenna is proposed for applications in 5G communication. The proposed designed has the advantages of reduced size and fabrication cost as well as aids comparatively easier integration with future 5G enabled gadgets. The antenna is 30mm X 20mm X 1.67mm in dimension with Y-shaped feed on the upper surface and a defected ground plane (DGP) on the bottom. The proposed antenna geometry offers an operating bandwidth of 15.2% (i.e. 3.28- 3.82GHz) and a VSWR below 2. Also, a double-Y shaped multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for smartphone applications is introduced. The S-parameters (S11 and S22) are found to be below -10dB in 3.33-3.73GHz range. The antenna provides high gain, good radiation pattern and Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) below 2. Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC), Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC) and Directivity Gain (DG) are found to be below 0.01, below-6dB and above 9.99 respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Half Mode SIW Based Power Divider for Ku-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design for a highly compact half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) power divider is proposed. To improve the isolation, a triangular-shaped slot is etched in the bottom layer of the HMSIW. To validate the proposed concept, equal power divider (PD) is designed, fabricated and tested. The size of the HMSIW prototype is 0.13λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the guided wavelength. The proposed design operates at 12.7 GHz with the fractional bandwidth of 69.45% and the isolation achieved is 6 dB. The fabrication measured result is in good agreement with the simulated one.

articleTitle: 4K UHD Video Streaming and Gigabit Data to an Unreachable Smart Home Using Millimeter Wave Radio
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: IoT enabled devices, Computers, and Communication and their integration are making our home smarter with the support of 1Gbps internet speed. This is realized using Fiber to The Home (FTTH) Technology. The Author is working towards the solutions to two problems of FTTH and IoT enabled Smart Home. Millimeter-wave 28 GHz radio relaying of fiber signals to fiber unreachable homes is the solution to problem 1 of FTTH. The inclusion of Edge computing within the home and its local control to NB IoT based smart bulb is toward the solution to Problem 2 of Internet distribution within the home. In this way, the paper is attempting to integrate all the three IoT, Computer and Communication.

articleTitle: Mapping and Prediction of Urban Area with Markov-CA Model using Landsat-8 Images for Effective Management of Urban Area in Prayagraj City
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Study of land use land cover for changes and prediction of changes is one of the thrust areas in remote sensing. The present study deals with the changes in urban area with the help of temporal data available through Landsat-8 satellite for Prayagraj city. A Markov model assisted by cellular automata has been used to analyze the changes in the urban area using the images of the year 2013 through 2018 and predict the growth in urban area for the year 2023. The successive changes in urban area have been examined which deduce that the urban area has continuously grown in the region, however its growth is not monotonic. Since the study area is fixed in terms of the number of pixels, the successive growth of urban area is a result of shrinking of some other kind of land cover. It has been investigated in the study and observed that the urban area grown at the cost of land and vegetation areas as expected. The predicted map of the year 2023 has been obtained as a preliminary analysis of the data using Markov-CA model which shows that the results are promising and need more refinements to predict the exact growth. The work is useful for urban planning, especially the planning and development of smart cities for the future.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Front-End Circuits at 47 GHz using Additive Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper uses Polylactic Acid (PLA) used in 3D printing as a dielectric medium in Non-Radioactive Dielectric waveguide (NRD). Front-end circuits like 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order filter were designed and simulated with NRD to waveguide transition using horn antenna at 47 GHz. The simulations have been done using HFSS 17.1. The advantage and shortcomings of PLA made using additive printing technology like 3D printing is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Seasonal Variation of Day and Night Land Surface Temperature with Normalized Difference Vegetation Index using MODIS Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Urban heat island (UHI) is referred to the urban areas with temperatures higher than the neighbouring suburban or rural areas. The LST-NDVI relation shows negative relation in agricultural region but the relation may vary in heterogeneous urban areas. The day and night LST map was obtained for summer, winter and post-monsoon season and found that UHI effect was significant during night time over the seasons. The day LST shows UHI effect only during winter season. The present study focuses on the relation of LST with NDVI for both day and night time during winter, summer and post-monsoon seasons. The relation of day LST with NDVI was found nonlinear for summer and monsoon season whereas good negative linear relation was observed for winter (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>= 0.88). The night LST shows negative relation with NDVI in the three seasons but very good correlation was observed in winter (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>= 0.92). Therefore, the relation of LST with NDVI show negative relation when UHI effect was observed.

articleTitle: Extraordinary transmission analog for enhancing radiation from an electrically small radiator
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: An extraordinary transmission analog for strongly enhancing radiation from an electrically small radiator in the microwave regime is proposed in this paper. The electrically small radiated used here is a chip inductor loaded open coplanar monopole type antenna. EOT is achieved by implementing evanescent amplification using mu negative metamaterial placed symmetrically on both sides of the antenna. Near-field and far-field probing reveal that the mu negative split ring resonator not only amplifies the evanescent high spatial spectrum existing in the near-field of the antenna but also responsible for evanescent to propagation conversion.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Performance of Ionospheric Models with NavIC Observations during Geomagnetic Storms
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The paper presents an assessment of the performances of the global empirical models: International Reference Ionosphere (IRI)-2016 and the NeQuick2 model derived ionospheric Total Electron Content (TEC) with respect to the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC)/ Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System(IRNSS) estimated TEC under geomagnetic storm conditions. The present study is carried out over Indore (Geographic: 22.52°N 75.92°E and Magnetic Dip: 32.23°N, located close to the northern crest of the Equatorial Ionization Anomaly (EIA) region of the Indian sector). Analysis has been performed for an intense storm (September 6-10, 2017), a moderate storm (September 26-30, 2017) and a mild storm (January 17-21, 2018) that fall in the declining phase of the present solar cycle. It is observed that both IRI-2016 and NeQuick2 derived TEC are underestimates when compared with the observed TEC from NavIC and therefore fail to predict storm time changes in TEC over this region and requires real data inclusion from NavIC for better prediction over the variable Indian longitude sector.

articleTitle: Pre-monsoon Study of Aerosol Parameters and Particulate Matters over Varanasi for 2017
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Aerosol characteristics over Varanasi region during pre-monsoon (April - June) period were analyzed for year 2017. Aerosol optical properties and angstrom exponent were measured using MICROTOPS-II Sunphotometer. The mean AOD for the period of study was found to be 0.78 where as mean angstrom exponent (AE at 440 - 870 nm) was found to be 0.29. Average concentrations of PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> and PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> were found to be 38.15 ± 22.48 µg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and 126.10 ± 45.39 µg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> respectively, which clearly demonstrates dominance of coarse mode particles particularly in this season.

articleTitle: Design of a Printed Triangular Patch Antenna Loaded with Novel Trident-Shaped Metasurface and Defected Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Printed metasurface antenna has emerged as the most prominent antenna structure in the emerging wireless technologies. This paper proposes the design of a compact, high gain metasurface antenna (MSA) in which the triangular patch antenna has been used as a radiating element. The conventional patch is loaded with a novel trident shaped metasurface (MS) to enhance the performance of the antenna exhibiting a penta-band operating characteristics. The proposed MSA also introduces defected ground and microstrip structures to improve the bandwidth. The proposed antenna resonates at 6.68 GHz, 9.21 GHz, 10.91 GHz, 11.50 GHz and 11.92 GHz respectively, having the highest realized gain of 11 dBi making it suitable for wireless system designs for satellite communication (X-band), defense applications and 5G communications.

articleTitle: Graphene-based metasurface for wideband linear to circular polarization conversion
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper deals with a brief development of an optimized graphene-based metasurface for wideband polarization conversion from incident linearly polarized wave to circularly polarized wave in the lower mid-infrared region. The introduction of specifically designed graphene patterns on the two complementary sides of a silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) substrate provides circular polarization conversion (CPC) between 5 THz and 9 THz. The Stokes parameters have been calculated for the validation of the output circularly polarized (CP) wave. The proposed device is designed in the sub-wavelength region with a thickness of around λ/6.12 and periodicity of λ/5.71.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Coplanar Stripline fed Dual Band Monopole as Radiolytic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A dual frequency omnidirectional monopole antenna design with a gain better than 2dBi at both bands is proposed in this paper for the detection of ions during the radiolysis process. The proposed antenna is able to detect with a high level of accuracy H+ and OH- ions formed during the process radiolysis. Dual band is achieved by configuring the ground plane to generate different electrical length corresponding to desired operating frequencies. The design ensures compactness, low cost and high efficiency in the mentioned scenario and the proposed antenna could be a valid alternative to standard radiation leakage detectors.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cross-Coupled Bandpass Filter With Wide-Stopband
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents a fourth-order cross-coupled bandpass filter with wide-stopband designed using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavities. The fundamental TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> mode of the cavity is utilized to constitute the passband. The cross-coupling topology is adopted to realize two transmission zeros (TZs) at both sides of the passband which improve the filter selectivity. Moreover, the passband generated by the first higher-order mode of the cavity TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf> is suppressed by minimizing its coupling in order to obtain wide-stopband rejection. The designed filter is fabricated and measured in order to validate the present approach. The simulation and measurement results show an acceptable agreement between them.

articleTitle: Prospective Design of Dual Band Graphene-Based Patch Antenna for Mid-THz Band
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, we have presented a dual-band graphene patch antenna for mid-THz application. The antenna comprises of two rectangular slots in a single graphene layer, which is placed on the top of metal-backed SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> dielectric. The antenna is fed with proximity feed and it operates at two different frequencies viz., 1.27 THz and 4.08 THz. It gives a wide bandwidth of 0.4 THz and 0.3 THz with minimum reflection coefficient of -41 dB and -28 dB at frequencies 1.27 THz and 4.08 THz, respectively. The maximum realized gain of the proposed antenna is 4.95 dB at lower frequency and 3.81 dB at higher frequency and shows 89% and 86% efficiencies at both lower and upper frequencies. This antenna can find its application in filed like spectroscopy, defense, indoor communication, etc.

articleTitle: Modified Clover Arranged Reactively Loaded Dual Band Polarization Agile Omnidirectional Wire Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Major limitation of planar (microstrip) antenna is its inability to provide omni-directional radiation patterns. Base station trans-receiver antennas for mobile communication require omni-directional radiation patterns. In this report an efficient four looped modified and reactively loaded clover arranged omni-directional polarization agile (circularly polarized in lower band an d dual polarized in higher band) wire antenna has been presented for dual band viz. mobile communication and WiMAX frequency operations.

articleTitle: Effect on Aerosol Optical Depth during Diwali Festival in Varanasi, India
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The present study is focused on the variation of aerosol optical depth (AOD) and chemical properties during Diwali festival over Varanasi (25.27° N, 82.99° E). AOD is taken using ground based as well as satellite based observations using MICROTOPS-II and MODIS, respectively. The elemental components are analyzed using Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) Coupled with Energy Dispersive X-ray Microanalyzer (EDX) analysis. Analysis of particulate matters (PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf> and PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>) is done using high volume samplers, ground based observations. All the observations are divided in to three parts i.e. PreDiwali, Post-Diwali and Diwali event. AOD is found to be enhanced on Diwali day as huge amount of fire crackers are used by the peoples. Enhancement in AOD is observed by both ground based and satellite based observations. Enhancements in the elements are also found like carbon, silicon, sodium. However other elements like oxygen, aluminum, potassium, fluorine, zinc, chlorine were also found in the atmosphere.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gain Substrate Integrated Waveguide H Plane Horn Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper proposed the concept of using metallic via in the H-plane SIW horn antenna to enhance gain. The simulated antenna works for K-band and Ka band applications. Simple SIW horn antenna shows the simulated gain of 5.918dB. The peak gain achieved for the optimized designed is 7.123dB at 29.11GHz frequency. The results of via introduction to H-plane horn antenna are compared for two different configurations.

articleTitle: Inter-Comparison of satellite retrieved Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) from geostationary and polar-orbiting platforms with ground-based measurements over a Semi-continental site of north-eastern India
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In the area of global climatic implications of atmospheric aerosols in the recent decades, accurate estimation of aerosol properties on long-time basis over distinct geographic regions and seasons are very essential In this regard, satellite remote sensing is an effective tool to monitor Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), a parameter most important for assessing the radiative impact of aerosols, at the regional as well as global level. This study aims at comparing the satellite retrieved AOD from geostationary and polar-orbiting platforms with the ground-based measurements over the semi-continental site of northeastern India. For this, we have utilized AOD products derived from the imager of Indian National Satellite (INSAT)-3DR and the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro Radiometer (MODIS) on-board Terra and Aqua satellites. A handheld Sun Photometer (Microtops-II) provided the ground based estimates of AOD. The main goal is to validate and demonstrate the most accurate and suitable satellite retrieval of aerosols over the northeastern semi-continental site of India. In the present study, we used INSAT-3DR AOD observations at 650 nm over the region of interest and the level-3 daily AOD estimates from MODIS (both Aqua and Terra) at the same wavelength for the year of 2015. The inter-comparison of satellite retrieved AOD with ground based AOD is examined and statistical parameters, such as root mean square error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) are determined for each set of data in different time blocks. Overall, MODIS on-board the polar orbiting platforms (aqua and terra) showed better correlation with the ground based sun-Photometer measurements. On the other hand, even though the bias in AOD retrieval from geostationary platform is higher than that of the polar orbiting ones, the diurnal features of aerosol were clearly visible in the INSAT-3DR data. This is important in order to understand the distinct influence local and synoptic source processes.

articleTitle: Study the Ionospheric Total Electron Content (TEC) variation during Geomagnetic Storm in 24th Solar Cycle
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: We have used the IGS (International Geodesic Survey) dual frequency GPS data of the Indian IGS Station IISC, Bangalore to investigate the Total Electron Content (TEC). We used the TEC to study the geomagnetic storms variation of the ionosphere at IISC, Bangalore ((13.02°N, 77.57°E)), a low latitude region in the India. We used four years of data (2014-2017) to study the magnetic quiet and storm time variation. The diurnal variation of TEC is maximum for 2014 and then decreased (2015-2017) to a minimum. The diurnal TEC attains a maximum value at the afternoon (13:00-17:00 IST) for 2014-2017, that is not symmetrical about the noon. We also see that for seasonal variation of for value TEC is maximum for March equinox. During storm time, TEC has increased in comparison with quiet day TEC. Both negative and positive stroms are observed during this period. During the negative storm there is sharp decrement in TEC on the next day of the geomagnetic storm. The change in TEC on storm day is between 19-44%.

articleTitle: PIC simulation study of dielectric-filled S-band magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO)
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, S-band dielectric-filled magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) has been designed and simulation has been performed using 3D PIC code ‘CST’. The dielectric-filled MILO is a new kind of HPM device having slow wave structure partially filled with low-loss dielectric to enhance the overall efficiency. The device design methodology follow the similar step of conventional MILO. To validate the designed structure, beam-absent simulation performed using Eigenmode solver to find dispersion curve. Finally, with the beam parameters: 600 kV voltage and 45 kA current, a high power microwave of ~4 GW peak power at 2.57 GHz frequency generated in TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode. The efficiency of the device obtained is 14.8%.

articleTitle: Compact, Low-cost, Single-frequency NavIC Receiver Development
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems are being increasingly used for myriads of applications. Along with many global systems, various regional systems are also deployed to exploit commercial potential, for strategic point of views and self-reliance. IRNSS/ NavIC is one of such regional systems developed by ISRO. NavIC enabled, costly, geodetic receivers are available in market and at the same time, few NavIC enabled chipsets also are being offered by manufacturers. These NavIC chips are low cost but the associated receiver board costs are much higher in comparison to the chipsets. Compact, cost-effective NavIC receiver boards are essential for NavIC based application development, popularization and effective utilization of the system. This manuscript presents an effort towards development of a compact, cost-effective NavIC receiver board and the results on the solution accuracy obtained from it. The power-efficient board operates in L5 band and is of 8 cm  10 cm size. The module is working properly both in static and dynamic operation and can provide meter level 2-dimensional precision; the altitude variation is found to be higher in comparison. Final cost of the prototype board is less than US$ 60 which may be reduced during bulk production. The board can be used with Raspberry Pi (RPi) or other controller boards for ASCII NMEA data reception, display and recording. The board has the potential for using it as a stand-alone receiver, for integration with other systems towards application development or as a geolocation sensor in IoT applications enhancing the possibility of deployment of multiple sensors because of cost, power and size efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Wideband Stacked Isosceles Triangular DRA
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A stacked wide band DRA of isosceles triangular shape, having bandwidth from 4.374 GHz to 7.65 GHz (covering the C band communication channel) is designed and analyzed in this paper. The primary contribution of the work lies in deriving a closed form equation for the resonant frequencies of TM mode of the stack. This helps in identifying the design parameters to obtain the wide band. Moreover, the radiation patterns are broadside throughout the frequency range, as the first three TM mode frequencies get merged to produce the wide band.

articleTitle: Modeling the Ionosphere Using Extended Spherical Harmonics Approach for Generation of IRNSS/NavIC based Precise Ionospheric Maps/Products (NPIM) over Indian Region
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: IRNSS (Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System)/NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) is a regional satellite based navigation system over Indian region being developed by Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). There are many error sources affecting the navigation performance of satellite based navigation systems. Among them, the error due to ionosphere is the pre dominant source of error especially while working with radio frequencies in real time as well as in post processing mode for areas of ionospheric research. In real time mode, ionospheric error corrections are available to users as broadcast ionospheric corrections for single frequency users and frequency dependent advantage for dual frequency users to correct the ionospheric delay in their line of sight. But there are some applications where precise ionospheric corrections are required in post processed mode for their scientific research and analysis which is a global requirement over equatorial region which is more prone to ionospheric anomalies and high ionospheric variations. Precise ionospheric products in general provide precise total electron content (TEC) values for the identified grid points over the globe at a specified height above the earth considering a thin shell approximation of the ionosphere. These precise ionospheric products are usually generated by monitoring the ionosphere using ground station network ranging to navigation satellites orbiting the earth i.e., GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) data. A perfect example is the Global Ionosphere Maps (GIM) generated using IGS (International GNSS Service) stations network. In this paper, effort has been made to generate precise ionospheric products similar to GIM using NavIC ionospheric data for grid points identified over Indian region. A novel technique based on spherical harmonics with an extended polynomial fit is designed for generating NavIC based Precise Ionospheric Maps (NPIM). The generated NPIM over Indian region using this technique is then compared and evaluated with GIM data over Indian region. It is found that NPIM provides better accuracy of 2 to 4 TECU (TEC units) as against 5 to 6 TECU by GIM data over Indian region.

articleTitle: Compact microstrip Wideband Band Stop Filter with folded stubs to increase coupling
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This work presents a new type of wide band stop filter (BSF). The proposed filter topology consists of folded stubs, which controls band stop range. The filter characteristics can be easily controlled by the length of stubs and folded stubs can control coupling between two stubs. The proposed filter design has cut-off frequency of 2.3 GHz. Stopband rejection depth and bandwidth can be controlled by stubs width and spacing between stubs. Three zeros are present in stopband region. This proposed filter has 2.3 - 4.3 GHz band width with 20dB rejection. Sharp cut off rate is achieved 28.3dB per GHz frequency. The compact design structure has size of 15.48mm×29.6mm (0.16λg×0.31λg ) with port length.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement of Antenna Pair for Implantable Application
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A compact two element implantable antenna operating in 2.4 GHz ISM band with enhanced isolation is presented. The reduction of coupling between two implanted radiating elements in a human body environment is realized by placing a Meander line resonator as a decoupling element. Moreover, the mutual coupling between two antennas is studied and quantified by using a circuit model analysis. The proposed antenna features a very good miniaturization with the dimensions of 0.06λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.14λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.01λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free-space wavelength at operating frequency.

articleTitle: Stacked Pyramidal Shaped Half Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Wideband Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A novel stacked pyramidal shaped half cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna excited by probe feed is presented in this paper for wideband wireless applications. Here, the operating frequency bandwidth is enhanced by using two techniques namely stacking of two dielectric material and pyramidal stepped shape arrangement. It offers low base area for the DRA in contact to the ground plane. Proposed antenna offers operating frequency range from 3.7 GHz - 9 GHz with 6.2 dBi maximum gain for numerous wireless application such as WiMAX, Satellite, military etc. Near field modes namely TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12δ</inf> are investigated.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis for Effective Cooling of a Millimeter-wave Mirror
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Thermal analyses were carried out for a millimeter-wave mirror taking three different ways of surface heat load: i) over the full front reflecting surface of the mirror, ii) over the circular cross section (diameter 63.5mm) similar to that of RF beam over the front reflecting surface of the mirror, and iii) over the circular cross section (diameter 63.5mm) in Gaussian profiled manner on the front reflecting surface of the mirror. The thermal images were analyzed and the values of highest temperature attained and their location over the mirror were monitored. The highest temperature attained in three cases of heat load are 348.72, 330.53 and 391.64°C, respectively. Under practical consideration of Gaussian heat load, the maximum temperature attained was found below the allowable maximum temperature limit of 400°C and thus the proposed cooling found to be adequate for the case of heat load of 5kW.

articleTitle: Systematic Investigation of Silicon Micromachined Waveguide Structure & Designing Passive Components out of it for THz Application
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this article, a detailed study of Silicon micromachined based rectangular waveguide and various passive components for terahertz (THz) application is reported. Effect of various process parameters on the performance of these components is studied using a commercial EM solver and a comparative analysis is performed with all previously reported models. WR-2.2 based passive devices have been designed for 300 to 400 GHz band. Multiple passive devices require waveguide bends, which directly affects the phase information of signal. Bend design demands highly precise parameter selection at these higher frequencies which has been elaborated in this article. Using this bend optimization, two distinct passive devices, namely, Directional Couplers (7, 10 and 13 dB) and Multi-hole branch line hybrid have been designed for THz band.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Wide-Band Multi-Disc RF Window for Gyrotron Travelling Wave Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Multi-disc RF window has been designed to increases bandwidth capabilities, provides minimum reflection and maximum transmission. The RF propagation characteristics of single disc and multi-disc RF window have been discussed using the CST Microwave Studio (MWS) and HFSS. The comparative study of multi-disc RF window predicted the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of (<-20 dB) and (>-0.07 dB), respectively over the frequency range of 8 GHz to 12 GHz. The present study of multi-disc RF window predicted the bandwidth of 4 GHz, which is the eight times higher than the bandwidth of single disc RF window.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarisation Discrimination (XPD) Model due to Rain at 20 and 30 GHz LOS Link for Indian Tropical Climate
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The spatial and temporal characteristics of rainfall and raindrop size distribution for terrestrial or space to earth communication link affects the perfromace of radio and radar communication system operating above 10 GHz in the temperate climate and above 7 GHz in tropical and equatorial climate. The rain drop size distribution plays an important role for limiting the performance of communiation system due to different rain attenuation and polarization of radio signals at mm wave rfequuencies. The single point measurement of rainfall rate as well as rain drop distribution, and non-uniform rainfall rate characteristics of terrestrial radio link causes difference in the rain attenuation measured value at mm wave frequencies from the rain attenuation based on raindrop size distribution or rainfall rate. In this paper, model for cross-polarisation discrimination (XPD) due to rain rate at 20 GHz and 30 GHz have been developed based on rain attenuation measurement of LOS link for vertical and horizontal polarisation signals. The variation of XPD with rain rate and co-polar attenuation have been discussed for understanding the effect of rain drop size distribution at 20/ 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling & Simulation of 2-D Metamaterial Reflector Lens Antenna for Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This work is dealing with the principle of modelling a 2-D metamaterial reflector lens antenna used as a communication device. The lens antenna is consisting of low loss with wideband E-shaped metamaterial resonators (ESR) and the parabolic reflector. The metamaterial structure shows a negative refractive index (NRI) behaviour to a normally incident wave. The numerical simulation has been carried out using CST microwave studio (MWS) 3-D simulator. The main idea of this present work is to investigate the focusing effect of the planar metamaterial lens and to enhance the radiation pattern by reducing the sidelobe levels and increasing the main lobe level. The simulated results of both far-field and near-field radiation patterns in wider bandwidth, showing high directivity and gain upto 18dBi is achieved.

articleTitle: Slit Loaded E-Shaped Single Layer Broadband Rectangular Patch Antennas with High Gain and Low Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A simple single layer broadband rectangular patch antenna (RPA) having improved radiation and input performances is presented.
