Here, an air gap loaded E-shaped RPA with double slits on patch surface has been investigated. It reveals wide impedance bandwidth of 30% at 1.97 GHz. Also, the gain of present antenna is more than 3 dB higher than that of conventional RPA working at same frequency. Around 9.8 dBi gain is reveled from present simple single layer RMA. Notably, an excellent polarization purity of 25 dB is achieved from present RPA. The antenna efficiency of 97.8% is obtained. The IE3D simulation software based on Method of Moments (MoM) is used for simulation.

articleTitle: Design of helix slow wave structure for X band helix TWT using multi-dispersion
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a compact, multi dispersive helix slow-wave structure (SWS) with coaxial input coupler for a high efficiency X-band helix TWT has been proposed. Design of SWS has been carried out using in-house developed analytical code GANGA, SUNRAY-1D and commercial software ANSYS Electronics Desktop. The helix SWS has been modelled in three sections each having different dispersion characteristics – realized by different loading scheme to each section to achieve desired output characteristics. Due to different dispersion characteristics, coupling system has also been suitable modelled to exchange RF power from SWS.

articleTitle: Modeling of electrically tunable metamaterial embedded intersubband transitions in GaN HEMT for terahertz applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents the computational study of the combined metamaterial driven inter-sub band transition phenomenon in GaN HEMT which is possible mode to extend its operating frequency well beyond its present cutoff frequency to THz band. It has been reported that the device dimension and geometry act as terahertz (THz) metamaterial and its couple with two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) inside triangular quantum well of HEMT. Semiconductor device modeling has been used to extract intersubband (ISB) resonance phenomena by solving Schrodinger- Poisson equations self-consistently and k.p method. Terahertz response of entire GaN HEMT device has been modeled using Finite difference frequency domain electromagnetic simulation for 0.3 to 3.0 THz region. The combination of external electrical field dependent tunable ISBT and metamaterial driven enhancement of electric field distribution inside channel due to THz illumination clearly explain the GaN HEMT device behavior at THz frequency

articleTitle: Estimation of Total Electron Content using NavIC Signals
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) formerly known as Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) provides geo-spatial positioning with regional coverage over Indian landmass extended upto 1500 km. In general, NavIC have three main segments, namely the space segment, the ground segment and the user segment. NavIC satellites broadcast the signals in two different frequencies namely S (2492.045 MHz) and L5 (1575.42 MHz) using which the users can find out its position using an appropriate receiver. The positional accuracy of NavIC user is limited by several sources of errors of which the most predominant error is due to ionosphere which is a function of electron density represented by the total electron content (TEC). In order to get the precise user position, it is necessary to estimate this delay correctly and compensate during position estimation. In this paper, an attempt is made to understand the behaviour of the ionosphere delay using the NavIC signals. Since the ionospheric electron density varies with geographical coordinates and time, the behavior of ionosphere in terms of Total Electron Content is studied using the measurements observed from the NavIC receiver at different laltitude over Indian region. As the NavIC receiver produces two types of measurements, viz. code and carrier phase with the former being an unambiguous measurement but with more measurement noise while the later as ambiguous but precise measurements. A software module has been developed to resolve this ambiguity and compute the TEC. A comparison between the TEC using the code measurements and carrier measurements after integer ambiguity resolution is presented.

articleTitle: Detection of Coronal Holes Using Hough Simulated Parameterized Online Region-Based Active Contour Method
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper a novel technique of Hough transformed simulated parameterized online region-based active contour method (PORACM) has been proposed for the real-time detection and extraction of coronal holes (CHs) in solar disk (SD) image without disturbing resolution of the image. For the purpose a circular contour based on Hough transform has been initialized on the SD image. Now based on the formulation of PORACM the initialized circular contour is made to move towards the boundary of the desired region. At the final stage when the contour position does not change any more is considered as the final contour and the region inside contour is extracted as the CHs of the given SD image. The proposed technique has been implemented on benchmark SD images and has been compared with the available work on CHs detection. The generated results shows capability of the proposed technique in detection and extraction of CHs in SD image.

articleTitle: Seasonal Variability of Atmospheric Aerosols over Varanasi Region during 2010-2016
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The role of atmospheric aerosols in climate and climate change is one of the largest uncertainties in understanding the present climate and in capability to predict future climate change. Due to which, the study of optical properties of atmospheric aerosols were conducted for seven years to see the massive aerosol loading and its seasonal variability using satellite data obtained from MODIS. In the present study AOD was analyzed for the year 2010-2016 using satellite data obtained from MODIS Terra for different seasons. The mean AOD for Winter, Pre-monsoon, Monsoon and Post-monsoon were found to be 0.73, 0.46, 0.37, and 0.72 respectively. Highest value of AOD was found during winter season and lowest during Monsoon season. Similarly respective mean angstrom coefficient for winter, Pre-monsoon, Monsoon and Post-monsoon were found to be 1.48, 0.71, 1.28, and 1.36.

articleTitle: Single Chip Broadband Testset for Network Analyzers
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of single chip broadband testset for portable network analyzers. This testset is designed using divider combiner technique. The testset is comprised of an out of phase divider circuit, an intermediate matching network and an in phase combiner circuit. The testset measures the reflection coefficient of an arbitrary load. It has one port for input, second port for arbitrary load (DUT), third and fourth port for reflected and reference power detectors by which we can measure S-parameters of DUT. The testset shows high isolation and dynamic range over broad bandwidth. The dynamic range of the testset is 10 dB to 49.9 dB over frequency range from 1.7 GHz to 12 GHz. The design advantage is, it is an on chip design with area coverage 3.2 × 3.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Due to its single chip design it is suitable for compact, portable network analyzers for field testing applications. The design has been realized using UMC 180 nm RF/MM CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of planar and spherical cathodes in gridded electron guns for Inductive output tubes
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Inductive Output Tube (IOT) is a vacuum electron tube capable of amplifying radio frequency (RF) power with high efficiency. It is popularly used as high power source in communication transmitters and particle accelerators operating at ultra-high frequency (UHF) band. The basic structure of IOT is similar to a Klystron except that the gun and input cavity are two distinctly separated components in Klystron whereas these two components are integrated together in case of an IOT which makes the electron gun and input cavity the most critical part to design and develop. The paper discusses the design results of two electron guns having different shapes of cathode emitting surfaces - spherical and planar. Both structures have been designed for same specifications and a comparative analysis has been presented. On the basis of the merits and demerits of these structures, the more preferable design has been pointed out to implement in IOTs.

articleTitle: High Gain Wideband Substrate Integrated (SIW) Slot Antenna with Horn Aperture for 5G
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slot antenna with horn aperturehas been proposed for 5G communication. It covers the wide bandwidth from 25.0 to 29.5GHz and it has maximum gain 13.1dB at frequency 28GHz. It has impedance matching of 16.51% (4.5 GHz). Presented antenna is compact in size and suitable for modern 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: Performance Estimation of ARIMA Model for Orographic Rainfall Region
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Performance of Auto regressive integrated moving average model (ARIMA) is evaluated for the prediction of highly stochastic time series of rainfall for an area which has a very significant topographical feature in causing orographic precipitation. Performance is calculated mainly on the basis of three important machine learning (ML) parameters Fit Percentage estimation (FPE), Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The model presented here shows minimum value of prediction error as a prediction of ten steps ahead.

articleTitle: Parasitically Coupled Microstrip Patch Antenna for DCS and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A novel parasitic microstrip patch antenna using direct electromagnetic gap coupling technique for DCS/WLAN applications is presented in this paper. The rectangular microstrip feed line is placed in between the parasitic radiators for dual band operations. The proposed antenna has dimensions of 70×70×4.8mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It is fabricated on FR4 substrate having the dielectric constant of 4.4 and loss tangent of 0.02. The prototype shows 2:1 VSWR bandwidth within frequency bands DCS (1710-1785 MHz) and WLAN (2400-2480 MHz). The proposed antenna exhibits the gain of 3.7 dBi in DCS band and 3.5 dBi in WLAN band.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis of ohmic quality factor of corrugated coaxial cavity structure for MILO
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Corrugated coaxial cavity structures are used as slow wave structure for magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO). The dispersion relation for electromagnetic wave propagation through different corrugated coaxial cavity structure has been calculated analytically and validated through simulation. Electromagnetic wave propagation through different structures has been estimated through commercial simulation software, ‘CST Microwave studio’. Furthermore, the electromagnetic analysis has been used to estimate the ohmic quality factor for different corrugated coaxial cavity structure. The results obtained through analysis compared with the simulation results and found with ~5% variation. The ohmic quality factor and EM wave propagation through different structures helps us to select the optimal corrugation coaxial cavity structure for MILO device.

articleTitle: Computation and Simulation of Cascaded Phase Noise for an FMCW Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In modern radar and communication systems, phase noise is one of the fundamental parameters to measure the performance. For such systems, phase noise can put a constraint on the minimum detectable signal level which must be returned from the target. So, it becomes crucial to measure the system phase noise accurately and realize the potential region of operation of radar. This paper presents the study of phase noise, its computation and simulation for a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar transmitter. The simulated result validates the theory and the computed result.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line Excited Wideband Millimeter Wave Bow-Tie Antenna
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a new excitation technique known as the Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line (SICL) technology for bow tie antenna operating in Millimeter wave (MM-wave) frequency. Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line provides wide bandwidth for TEM mode of operation. The Bow Tie antenna excited by SICL exhibits a wide 10 dB impedance bandwidth of 8.7 GHz with an average gain of 4.5 dBi in the entire frequency band. One advantage of using this new feeding technique is the elimination of balun as required in the microstrip technology to feed the antenna. Another advantage is the wideband nature of SICL that is difficult to be obtained with its counterpart namely, SIW (Substrate Integrated Waveguide). The end-fire radiation pattern of the proposed antenna shows co-polarization to cross polarization ratio of 13.7 dB at the center frequency. The antenna is suitable for 5G applications at millimeter wave frequencies beyond 24 GHz and applications at LMDS band.

articleTitle: Precise Time Transfer Through Optical Fibre Utilizing White Rabbit Network
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The present article describes an experimental study on precise and accurate time transfer through an optical fibre link for in house dissemination of time from an ultra-stable reference clock. The link consists of couple of single mode optical fibres and a White Rabbit (WR) link, using commercially available White Rabbit equipment along with necessary devices and software. We demonstrate time transfer accuracy remains well within 50 ps with respect to a primary clock over a very long period of time and the achieved link stability is about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> at 2000 sec integration time.

articleTitle: Design of High Gain Circularly Polarized 2×2 Single Feed Elliptical Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A design of an elliptical patch antenna array for circular polarization is presented. Single patch elliptical microstrip antenna has low gain which is improved by the use of single feed elliptical patch antenna array. The antenna array is designed at 2.8 GHz. It shows a gain of 9.825dB and axial ratio 2.045dB.

articleTitle: Compact coupled-line microstrip bandpass filter with spurious passband suppression using Minkowski fractal
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The present article exhibits the improvement in harmonic suppression of the compact third-order coupled-line Chebyshev bandpass filter centered at 2.5 GHz by Minkowski fractals. The harmonic suppression performance has been investigated for the symmetrically folded coupled-line filter by incorporating Minkowski fractals with proper indentation to the outer and coupled edges. Accordingly, the modal phase velocity compensation has been achieved by the space filling property of the fractals. More than 46 dB and 48 dB of stopband rejection levels along with a size reduction of more than 50% have been obtained experimentally for the filters with first and second order iteration of the fractals.

articleTitle: Shape Identification of Target Behind Wall Using Fourier Descriptor and Morphology
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Though-the-Wall Imaging Systems are promising candidates for search and rescue applications especially in the disaster areas, where victims are buried under collapsed walls. These applications require such systems to identify the shape of the target. Therefore, in this paper, a methodology to identify the shape of the target behind a wall has been presented. The developed methodology consists of data acquisition, 2D through-the-wall image formation of the target, feature extraction, and shape identification using neural network and image morphology technique. For this purpose, C-scan data in of 3.5GHz–5.5 GHz frequency range using SFCW radar was collected for different shapes of wooden and metallic targets. An effective training technique using image morphology has been used to increase the detection accuracy of the artificial neural network (ANN) model. From, the developed ANN model result the retrieved shape of the target was found to be in good agreement with original shape.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-based Vacuum Electronic Devices with Miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Metamaterial is a sort of new artificial constructed sub-wavelength structure. Unlike conventional composite materials, its electromagnetic characteristics are manipulated by its shape, size, arrangement, and materials. In this paper, based on reversed Cherenkov radiation and enhanced transition radiation, metamaterial-inspired vacuum electronic devices with miniaturization such as metamaterial-based reversed Cherenkov oscillators and extended interaction oscillators are developed. They maybe have important applications in the high power microwaves, accelerators, microwave heating, and so on.

articleTitle: DC Analysis of Space Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The electron trajectory, from electron gun to collector through helix, of traveling wave tube (TWT) with magnetic field in DC condition is analyzed. The electron beam from cathode in the electron gun is confined by the PPM focusing structure and traversed helix in the RF section and collected in the collector. This paper presents complete DC simulation of a TWT and minimization of helix interception current by optimizing magnetic field as well as with secondary emission in collector using OPERA simulation software.

articleTitle: Miniature Elliptical Waveguide Antenna Design Using Square Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: An open-ended Elliptical waveguide loaded with Square Split Ring Resonator (SSRR) performance is investigating under the cutoff frequency region. The main objective of this paper is to find its radiation pattern (open-end) below the cutoff frequency region. The simulation is carried out in commercially available FEM based software Ansys HFSS-16.

articleTitle: A preliminary study of Amplitude and Phase scintillation over the Indian permanent scientific GPS station to understand L1 signal propagation through the ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The irregular electron density structure in an ionospheric layer causes fluctuation in Amplitude and Phase of the trans-ionospheric L1 signal from GPS posing a major challenge to the Quality of Service. The variation of electron density structure in an Ionospheric layer causes the fluctuation of the trans-ionospheric radio wave signals over the sub-auroral ionospheric region. The GPS data from the Indian Permanent Scientific base "Maitri" (Geog70°76"S, 11°74"E) which is situated in Antarctica was considered for this study. The investigation shows significant fading of GPS signal due to such ionospheric irregular electron density structures.

articleTitle: Constraints on Line Parameter for the Practical Realization of DIFM: Electronic Warfare Receiver
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the RF delay line output parameters for the realization of a good electronic support measure (ESM) system which can fulfill the modern time requirements. To develop a precise system, delay line outputs should satisfy certain limiting criteria’s i.e. phase imbalance between I & Q data of delay line, Local Oscillator feed input phase difference between different mixers, phase variation w.r.t frequency, input power, & temperature for individual delay line. Apart from all these parameters, line ratio between the adjacent delay lines also need to be considered. The RF delay line system satisfy these criteria’s will be suitable for digital interface to achieve final highly precise frequency output.

articleTitle: IRI-2016 model results during solar cycle-24 at low latitude station Dhanbad using TEC and foF2
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The quit time ionospheric variability at low latitude station Dhanbad, India (Geog. Lat. 23.79N, Geog. Long. 86.43E) have been investigated for the period 2009-2018 that includes complete solar cycle-24. Our result showed solar activity interdependence of TEC and foF2 variation whose noontime values increase/decrease with the inclining/descending phase of the solar cycle. A presence of semiannual anomaly has also been perceived along with equinoctial asymmetry depending upon the phase of activity. Concerning the seasonal variation, local time effects have been ascertained.

articleTitle: Lattice Reduction Aided Receiver for mmWave Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) technology has been proven to be the solution for the demand of the future generation communication system. And it is continuously under development. For successful deployment of the 5G, mmWave MIMO system is going to play a decisive role. And this paper represents the performance of the mmWave MIMO system with lattice reduction aided non-linear receivers. The performance is evaluated by having the comparison with the conventional linear receivers.

articleTitle: Planar Asymmetric Single Split Left Handed Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The article presents a new Asymmetric Single Split Resonator (ASSR) for negative permeability metamaterial applications with frequency and bandwidth tuning and its characteristics. The proposed uniplanar structure is a modified form of popular symmetric double ring Split Ring Resonator (SRR) with a single split on the outer ring. The prototype is analyzed based on reflection and transmission coefficients and unit cell simulations. The asymmetry variation and the variation in coupling with split orientation are studied as a method to improve the bandwidth of the same which reveals it as a right candidate for metamaterial applications.

articleTitle: RF Energy Harvesting for GSM and Wi-Fi Band
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: To meet the ever-growing need for sustainable energy resources, abundant radio frequency (RF) electromagnetic (EM) waves kinetic energy could be used for energy harvesting. This paper gives an insight into the conversion of RF-EM waves into DC, which can be utilized further to power up low power devices. The required aim is achieved by designing a Rectenna (rectifier and antenna) matched together for the same band of frequencies. In the design, a new rectifier configuration based on 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> hybrid junction is prospected for the dual-band for GSM (1 GHz) and Wi-Fi (2.45 GHz) both. The dipole antenna and rectifier are designed as dual-band antenna and rectifier for Wi-Fi and GSM band giving an efficiency of 31% and 48%, respectively. To provide the circuit insight into behavior single band antenna and rectifier circuit designs are also explained.

articleTitle: A Superstrate-based Metasurface Antenna for Dual Band Application
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The design and performance of a superstrate-based metasurface (MS) antenna with defected ground has been reported in this paper for dual band application. The square annular shaped patch arranged in fractal manner acts as a radiating element. This antenna operates over dual frequency regions ranging from 8.28-8.62 GHz and 10.52-11.28 GHz with the respective fractional bandwidths of 4% and 7%. The antenna provides the maximum realized gain of 6.2 dBi at 10.89 GHz with endfire radiation pattern. The designed structure can be promoted for microimaging in medical analysis, satellite communication, defense and military applications.

articleTitle: Gain Enhanced Dual-Band Differential Fractal Slot Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A dual-band differential fractal slot antenna with enhanced gain for RF energy harvesting applications has been proposed in this paper. The antenna is designed to operate in frequency bands of UMTS (2.1 GHz), and WiMAX (3.3-4.1 GHz). The reflector directs the radiation in the forward direction, which results in an improvement in the gain, impedance matching, and reflection coefficient bandwidth of the two bands. The proposed antenna is designed, fabricated, and the results of the simulation and measurement are compared. The theoretical analysis of the proposed antenna is also carried out. The maximum gain of the antenna with the reflector at 2.18 GHz and 3.72 GHz frequency is more than 6 dBi. The antenna radiation efficiency of 62% and 84% are obtained for the UMTS and the WiMAX bands of operation, respectively.

articleTitle: On Nonpropagating Energy Around Antennas: Insights From the Theory of Radiation by Accelerated Charges
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: We provide an alternative viewpoint on nonpropagating energy around antennas different from the traditional reactive energy or the recently introduced Poynting localized approach. Instead of focusing on the infinitesimal dipole modelling (IDM) of current, or relying on the field-energy densities, we revisit the classic accelerated charge model of radiation to determine nonpropagating antenna energy involving distinct interactions between the velocity and acceleration fields. This approach can come in handy for analytical prediction of spacetime near-field energy dynamics around complex antenna systems and to probe deeper into the microscopic origins of energy and near-field dynamics close the source.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Patch Antenna with Compact CPW Feeding Network for L-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper T shaped microstrip monopole Antenna has been designed and proposed here for L band Applications. This proposed antenna structure involves a symmetric T slot concerning rectangular patch. The Results demonstrate that T Slot receiving antenna operated at frequency range from 1.2 to 1.7GHz, which is able to accomplish least voltage with great transmission capacity and radiation properties. Finally a Microstrip patch antenna working at full resonating frequency 1.5 GHz is designed. Operating frequency of the L band is in the range of 1 GHz to 2 GHz. Wavelength of L band from 30 cm to 15cm. Major Applications in the L-band are Radars , Radio , Telecommunication , Global positioning system(GPS) and Air Craft surveillance.

articleTitle: RASCAL: Reflector Antenna Efficiency, System Temperature, Sensitivity Computation purpose
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: For Reflector Antenna (Prime focus/ Cassegrain) is very important to know its overall antenna efficiency (the combination of aperture, spillover, feed efficiency), system temperature, and Sensitivity (in terms of G/Tsys). It is very difficult to Design a feed that has proper radiation pattern that gives good overall efficiency and minimum ground temperature, similarly for the receiver chain it is very difficult to get proper combination that gives minimum receiver temperature. For all this difficulty in the Reflector antenna we design and developed a software named RASCAL (Reflector Antenna Sensitivity CALculator). This software gives a quick response to the feed designer go or no go means the feed is suitable for the specific reflector similarly for RF engineer it will suggest that what are combinations will give lower receiver temperature. This software primarily used Radio Astronomy Instrumentation purpose, but this can be used in metrological as well as in RADAR engineering.

articleTitle: Human micro-Doppler intensity transformation for gait velocity estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The human gait micro Doppler signature includes the combined effect of human limb movements along with the main body translation. The decomposition of different components from human gait spectrogram is necessary to obtain the velocity information of human subject. A distance dependent, double threshold-based image transformation method has been adopted to extract out the torso Doppler frequencies from the joint time frequency spectrogram image in order to accurately estimate the actual instantaneous velocity of the human subject.

articleTitle: Design of Printed Dipole Antenna for Enhanced Coverage Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A four port dipole antenna array at sub-6 GHz band (3400-3600 MHz) for mobile phone application with enhanced coverage efficiency is presented in this paper. Here a method for characterizing multiple dipole antenna in a cellular handset has been introduced. Coverage efficiency is studied for the antenna topology for its performance analysis. The array consists of four antennas placed along the four edges of the substrate. The dipole antennas placed at the oppositely faced edges are similar in dimension i.e. antenna 1 & 3 and antenna 2 & 4 are of same dimension and thus the antenna in opposite locations radiate in same manner. A common ground plane is used at the center of the substrate to isolate the antennas and also reduces mutual coupling between the antennas. The ground plane also helps in increasing the gain of the antenna. The dipole antennas 1 and 3 exhibit a fractional bandwidth of 8.47% and gain of 3.8 dBi providing vertical polarization and the dipole antennas 2 and 4 exhibit a fractional bandwidth of 6.2% and gain of 6.1 dBi providing horizontal polarization. Thereby the proposed array covers most part of the azimuthal plane. This antenna system may find its application in 5G MIMO systems particularly in smartphone applications at sub-6 GHz band.

articleTitle: A Compact Multiband RF-Energy Harvesting System using Mutual Coupling Exploitation
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: RF-Energy is omnipresent at most of the places and its harvesting enables a non-ending source of energy for low power devices. It provides us a system which is self-sustainable in terms of power. A multi-band RF-Energy harvester is proposed in this paper. The Harvester is designed to work on WCDMA (3G) bands available in India: 0.9GHz and 2.1GHz and it also work in IMT-E band: 2.65GHz. Multiband MIMO patch antenna with two monopoles is used. Mutual coupling among patches of the antenna is used to enhance received power. The antenna is capable of receiving 74% of simulated power at 2.1GHz by utilizing mutual coupling effect. The proposed rectifier circuit is made using lumped elements, where Cockcroft-Walton voltage doubler is used with a single-stage full-wave rectifier. Impedance matching is done using capacitors and inductors.

articleTitle: Compact High Efficiency X-band Pulsed Helix-TWT for Airborne Radar
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper discusses the design and development of compact high-efficiency pulsed X-Band helix Travelling Wave Tube (TWT) delivering a minimum of 250W of peak output power over a bandwidth of 800 MHz with RF efficiency of 20% and minimum gain of 27 dB. Initial Electron-wave analysis was carried out using 1D-codes and was optimized using 3D PIC Solver in CST Studio. This TWT employs positive velocity taper near the output coupler in order to enhance RF interaction efficiency and reduce the second harmonic content at the output power from the device. The length of the SWS is around 95 mm with overall packaged TWT length of around 220 mm. Single stage depressed collector is used in the TWT and overall efficiency of 35% is achieved. Two prototype TWTs were developed and tested for performance.

articleTitle: A Unified Framework for Analysis of Polarimetric SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In the Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) literature, the approaches to coherent and incoherent data interpretation are bifurcated. In this paper, we present a Scattering Power Factorization Framework using a geodesic distance (for measuring dissimilarity between two Kennaugh matrices) to obtain scattering power components corresponding to input scattering models for an observation. It can be applied to both incoherent/coherent form of data, making it more universal in its approach. In addition, it is flexible with respect to the number of input models, and presents a non-negative splitting of total backscattered power across all polarimetric channels. It is demonstrated for its efficacy on a coherent data set containing a sub-scene of ALOS 2 L-band image near Singapore, and an incoherent data set of RADARSAT 2 C-band covering the city of San Francisco.

articleTitle: Modal Behavior of Circular Sector Microstrip antenna: A Necessary Revisit
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Circular sector microstrip antenna is revisited for two feed positions (along edge and centre positions). The effect of excitations of different modes as a function of feed location is discussed thoroughly. Also, the effect of feed location on polarizations of radiated field is summarized. Finally, an example of 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> CSMA is taken up to show the clear visual effect of feed location on input and radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Inspired Cavity backed CPW fed Dipole Slot Rectenna for UMTS and WiFi Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this work, a novel metamaterial inspired cavity backed Coplanar Waveguide (CPW) fed slot antenna is proposed for RF Energy Harvesting Applications. The antenna has been designed to operate at 2.16 GHz (UMTS Band) and 2.45 GHz (Wi-Fi) with the gain of 7.41 dB and 8.88 dB, respectively. The rectifying circuit has been matched directly at the input feed line of the antenna to give it a compact shape. The maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the proposed rectifying circuit using CPW technology is observed more than 60 % in both the operating bands with the load resistance of 1000 Ω at around 1 mw input power level.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Position Uncertainty in NavIC and GPS
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is system which uses satellites which allows users to determine their location and time up to a very high precision. Most common GNSS is Global Positioning System (GPS) developed by USA. India has recently developed its own GNSS called Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System (IRNSS). This paper analyses the uncertainty in position provided by IRNSS and GPS.

articleTitle: A study on multiple target resolving with in beam width using super resolution algorithmic approach in phased array radar
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Several studies have been proposed in literature discussing the resolvability of signals using several super resolution algorithms. But most of these literatures seldom discuss about the practical implementation issues and some of them are practically infeasible. This paper discusses more practical issues while combining radar signal processing with conventional super resolution technique specifically MUSIC. We are trying to migrate from conventional pencil beam scanning which is commonly used to resolve targets and look upon more practical aspects when we go deep into implementation using super resolution techniques in practical radar environments.

articleTitle: A physically realized timescale combining five Cesium atomic clocks
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Timescales are developed and maintained across various precise timing facilities for either metrological or navigation time-keeping. These timescales are generated using an ensemble of atomic clocks such as Cesium clocks and Active Hydrogen Masers (AHM). Theoretically, the ensemble output displays better frequency stability than any of the individual participating clocks. However, due to frequency corrections carried out during the physical realization of the same signal, the frequency stability is often not maintained. A timescale with an ensemble of five Cesium clocks was physically realized and compared to each of the participating clocks. It was observed that the ensemble output performs better than all the Cesium clocks and is close to its theoretical performance. The ensemble was implemented using the Kalman plus weights algorithm. In order to remove occasional spikes from the measurement data, an ARIMA (0, 1, 1) filter was used as a pre-filtering mechanism.

articleTitle: Design of Rectangular TE1,0 to Circular TE0,1 Mode Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A rectangular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,0</inf> to circular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,1</inf> mode converter was designed by simulation for the frequency band centered at 95 GHz using High Frequency Structure Simulator. The proposed design comprises of two parts: i) rectangular waveguide transition for TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,0</inf> to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,0</inf> mode and ii) rectangular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,0</inf> to circular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,1</inf> mode conversion. Part 1 was achieved in one section, however, part 2 was achieved in three sections: i) rectangular to square conversion, ii) square to elliptical conversion, and iii) elliptical to circular conversion. Coupling of energy from a mode at input port to the desired mode at output port was examined by analyzing the insertion loss characteristics corresponding to a mode at input port and the desired mode at output port. Thus, the dimensional parameters were optimized first for each independent parts and then all were cascaded to analyze the full assembly. The insertion loss of the designed mode converter is better than 1dB over 88-110 GHz, and the bandwidth is 19.7GHz (89.75 – 109.45 GHz) for allowed attenuation 0.5dB.

articleTitle: Gain Enhanced Quad-Band AMC Backed Printed Antenna with Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a gain enhanced quad band fractal based printed antenna backed with artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) has been proposed for S and C-band applications. The proposed antenna is designed to operate at 2.7 GHz, 4.84 GHz, 5.58 GHz and 5.9 GHz with highly realized gains of 8 dBi, 10.1 dBi, 6.9 dBi and 8.5 dBi respectively. The realized antenna provides narrow band impedance bandwidths of 40 MHz, 50 MHz, 55 MHz and 120 MHz in the four operating frequency bands. The ground, AMC unit cell, reflector sheet and the radiating patch of the antenna have been made using copper while Styrofoam has been used as the substrate material. Therefore, the proposed design is a promising candidate for low cost, high gain and multi-band structure mount antenna applications.

articleTitle: High Gain and Wideband Antenna using Metasurface Horn and Metasurface Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of high gain and wideband antenna by using the metasurface horn (MSH) and metasurface superstrate (MSS). Impedance matching bandwidth improves from 2.4% to 11.8% and gain improves from3.5dB to 9.3dB by adding metasurface horn (MSH) and metasurface superstrate (MSS). This technique can be useful for the design of the high gain antennas for the modern communication.

articleTitle: Neutral hydrogen distribution in the post reionization era through gravitational lenses
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Study of the evolution of neutral hydrogen (HI) in Inter-Galactic Medium during the post reionization era has the promise to understand the evolution of structure over cosmic time. The expected brightness temperature of the redshifted 21-cm line from the HI is rather low and hence direct observations are challenging. The synchrotron emission from our galaxy at the frequency of observation acts as a foreground to the cosmological signal. An additional challenge to detect the redshifted 21-cm signal is that this foreground is several orders of magnitude larger than the signal itself. We access the possibility of using strong gravitational lensing to enhance the 21-cm signal and detect it’s power spectrum at comoving scales of 4 Mpcs and lower at a redshift range of one to three. The added advantage of the lensing is that it only enhances the cosmological 21-cm signal and not the galactic synchrotron foreground. In this work we use a visibility based formalism to calculate the lensed power spectrum of the redshifted 21-cm signal. We show that the lensing modifies the telescope sampling function by magnifying the power spectrum at the observed visibility points in the baseline plane. We use available lens models from the optical study of galaxy clusters to estimate the modified sampling function. The result suggest lensing as a promising probe for the signal.

articleTitle: Surface Latent Heat Flux Anomaly: A thermal precursory effect of large Earthquake
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Earthquake is very vast, complicated, anisotropic process and its required multi-parametric approaches. It is very difficult task to predict precisely future earthquakes time, location and magnitude accurately from the observed precursory phenomena. The process related to earthquake and per-earthquake can create a significant level of thermal, mechanical and electrical perturbation in atmospheric and ionospheric layers through the so-called Lithosphere-Atmosphere-Ionosphere Coupling (LAIC. Thus any physical or chemical changes which are caused directly or indirectly from such a coupling can be used as a precursory tool to study seismic hazards. According to LAIC theory perseismic process stars few days prior to main shock of earthquake. There is radioactive ionization due to Rn-222 which emits from earthquake preparation zone. The so-called "Atmospheric plasma" is created due to this Radon emission from the cracks and faults near the preparation zone. Atmospheric plasma consists of electrons, molecular and complex ions, there are also aerosol particles which may be charged or neutral, cloud drops and precipitation drops, ice crystals and other impurities which actually distorting the classical structure of plasma. Atmospheric plasma forms long living ion complexes near ground layer of the atmosphere. The primary stage is the formation of near ground plasma in the form of long living ion clusters. This ion clusters are formed due to the ion-molecular reactions (after ionization by radon with water molecule in the near ground layer of the atmosphere. Ion attachment with the water molecule is an exo-thermic process and it left a huge impact in the normal trend of the air temperature. Attachment of water molecules to the newly formed ions also increase the latent heat. This enhancement of Latent heat is detected through various remote sensing tools like satellite as well as in many ground based instruments which measures surface air temperature, surface latent heat net flux, relative humidity and other atmospheric parameters. So for the investigation of the precursory phenomenon of the earthquake we chose satellite data of Atmospheric parameter namely Surface Latent Heat Flux. The possible relationship between the anomalous behavior of surface latent heat net flux during and prior to seismic events which occurred in Nepal on 25th April and 12th May, 2015 and in Kumamoto, Japan on 16th April, 2016 is studied here.

articleTitle: Plasma Waves in and around the Moon
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Plasma waves are observed in almost all the solar system objects such as planets, their satellites, comets and interplanetary medium. In planetary ionospheres, typical plasma density range is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> – 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and plasma temperature about 0.1 eV which is capable of sustaining plasma waves. A number of planetary satellites such as Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto of Jupiter and Saturnian satellites such as Titan, Enceladus and Rhea, are found to have plasma waves in their ionospheres. Earth’s natural satellite Moon, which has a tenuous atmosphere and even a more tenuous surface bound ionosphere, also support plasma waves around it. It is important to study the plasma waves as these waves play significant role in the dynamics of a space plasma system by controlling the scattering and loss of energetic charged particles and also provide information on solar wind-planet interactions, the energy distribution in plasma, etc. This paper summarizes the plasma waves observed in and around the Moon so far in the form of a brief review.

articleTitle: Extreme High-Q Resonant Transmission through Aperture Cavity Array
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this article, we present the simulation study of TeraHertz (THz) transmission through an array of rectangular apertures in subwavelength thick metal plate. We demonstrate that the resonance quality of the transmission through this perforated metal plate can be as high as Q~440 in Tera-Hertz (THz) frequency regime. Hence, this structure can be employed for very high resolution sensing. Furthermore, we present the electric field profiles, in order to understand the resonance mechanism of the structure.

articleTitle: Large scale coherent density and velocity structure measurement in the Interstellar medium of NGC 5236
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: We present here our preliminary results on measurement of H I coherent density and velocity structures in the ISM of external spiral galaxy NGC 5236. Our estimations are totally unbiased, as it is using moments of directly measured visibility from radio interferometer. Our result on density power spectrum estimation indicates the presence of scale invariant structures over a large length scales of two order of magnitude. Also our results suggest that the average scale height of NGC 5236 is less than 200pc. These result are giving insight to the generating mechanism behind the ISM turbulence which is still not known yet.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Double Side-cavity Gridless Reltron by Dual Extraction Sections
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Double side-cavity reltron is a recent advancement of the conventional reltron. Simulation-based studies have reported higher power capabilities and longer pulse duration in this kind of reltron. Here we have obtained the performance table of an S-band double side-cavity reltron with dual extraction cavity in terms of output power and efficiency. A conventional reltron is first modeled in CST microwave studio (MWS) to validate the experimentally reported results using Particle in cell (PIC) solver. Then the structure is modified to the double side-cavity type for obtaining the performance chart. The use of the dual extraction section results in a peak efficiency of 38%.

articleTitle: RF Propagation Characteristics of Y-shaped Coupler for Millimeter-Wave Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, the RF propagation characteristic of Y-shape input coupler for TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode 92 GHz gyro-TWT is presented. The input coupler converts the fundamental rectangular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode into desired circular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode of gyro-TWT through a Y-shape power divider. The input TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode is fed through the W-band rectangular waveguide (WR-10). A pill-box window is also used to isolate the vacuum inside the circuit from the outside atmospheric pressure. The CST simulation results predicts that input coupler offers a good transmission and low reflection (below -15 dB) over the frequency range of 88-100 GHz.

articleTitle: Aperiodic Metasurface for Broadband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, a straightforward design technique is presented for designing broadband, polarization-insensitive meta-surface for wideband radar cross-section (RCS) reduction. Two different unit cell structures, one dual resonance unit cell composed of a circular patch and circular loop and, a square patch are selected for enhancing the phase bandwidth and covering 2π range. Three different metasurfaces i.e. triangular checkerboard metasurface, random triangular checkerboard metasurface and aperiodic metasurface are designed and characterized. Enhanced performance, both in terms of diffused reflection and wideband RCS reduction, is achieved by aperiodic metasurface compared to the other two metasurfaces. The proposed aperiodic metasurface significantly reduce the RCS for wide operational bandwidth and demonstrate features such as polarization insensitivity and low design complexity.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of seasonal and diurnal variations of lower ionospheric reflection parameters based on IRI model
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Very Low Frequency (VLF) remote sensing technique is used to probe the D-layer modeling for which we use a very conventional model known as Wait<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>s 2-component ionospheric model. This model is characterized by two ionospheric parameters which are ‘steepness parameter’ (β) and ‘effective reflection height’ (h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>). International Reference Ionosphere (IRI 2012) model is an empirical standard model of the ionosphere, based on all available data sources. In this paper, we compute an electron density profile of the ionospheric D-layer by using IRI model under an ionospheric quiet condition for the year 2016 from altitude range 65 km to 85 Km at the VLF reception station IERCOO/ICSP, Sitapur [Lat 22.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup> N, Lon 87.48<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup> E]. By numerically best fitting, we compare it with Wait<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>s empirical formula. Using an auto-generated process we repeat this procedure for several times and computed an authorized data set of Wait<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>s parameters (β and h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup>) for four locations viz. Kolkata, Kathmandu, Pune, and Bhuj for the different time of the day and for the entire year. Using linear equation as a best fit to the altitude profile, we try to compute the actual data set of β and h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">′</sup> for the entire path of the various location of India and its subcontinent for VTX (18.2 kHz) transmitter for summer (July, 2009) and winter (December, 2008) period. By this data set, we showed the seasonal and diurnal variation of these two characteristic parameters behaviors and also using these parameters and Long Wavelength Propagation Capability (LWPC), we generate a spatio-temporal profile of simulated VLF signal amplitude for several baselines.

articleTitle: A wideband metamaterial absorber based on multiple interference model for mid-infrared applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: An ultrathin wideband metamaterial absorber based on multiple reflection interference model has been reported in this paper. The structure exhibits more than 95% absorption in the mid-infrared region extending from 5.6 µm to 7.1 µm. The absorption mechanism has been demonstrated based on the formation of Fabry-Perot resonance inside the dielectric cavity. The amplitude and phase conditions required for minimum reflection and maximum absorption in the entire band of operation has been well demonstrated in this paper. The structure exhibits wideband absorptivity response by maintaining size compactness (λ/5) and ultra-thin property (λ/24).

articleTitle: Brazing Failure Analysis in Single-Insulator Multi-stage Depressed Collector of TWTs
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Travelling wave tubes (TWTs) are generally known for their broadband operation, high gain and high efficiency of ~60%. Typically for efficiency enhancement of the TWTs, multi-stage depressed collector (MDC) with multiple stages of depression are used. Although different technologies exist for collector development, singleinsulator MDC (SI-MDC) outperforms others in providing (i) high breakdown limits, (ii) reduced size and size, and (iii) simple fabrication. But, the major challenge in these SI-MDCs has been in achieving the hermetic braze joints. The SI-MDCs had been developing micro-leaks immediately after brazing operation. Here, in this work, the authors have performed multiphysics ANSYS simulations to systematically understand the root cause of failure occurring during the brazing operation of SI-MDC assemblies. Correspondingly, the authors have modified the feedthrough connections to eliminate the excessive stress developing at the feedthrough pins, which was identified to be the root cause. The modified SI-MDC hasresulted in hermetic brazing joints validating the failure analysis. The detailed description about the simulation studies carried out to emulate the brazing process and their corresponding results are presented.

articleTitle: Information Transfer by Surface-Plasmon-Polariton Wave Propagating on Silver/Silicon Interface
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The limitations of both electronic and optical interconnects inside integrated circuits (ICs) may be overcome by interconnects in which information is transferred by pulse-modulated SPP waves guided by the planar interface of a metal and silicon. We simulated the evolution of a pulse carried by an SPP wave guided by a planar silver/silicon interface in the time domain. Evaluation of the Pearson correlation coefficient indicated that information can be transferred over long distances without significant loss of fidelity; thus, SPP-wave-based interconnects can act as effective conduits of information in ICs.

articleTitle: Convection Vertical Structure during dry and wet spells of Monsoon over the Western Ghats of India
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper uniquely characterizes the vertical structure of mesoscale convection during dry and wet periods of summer monsoon rainfall over the Western Ghats (WG) using time-continuous X-band radar observations and relates them to large scale environment. Echo top height (ETH) distribution exhibits bimodality (unimodality) during the dry (wet) period. Top heights of precipitating convection with low-level static stability, suggesting preponderance of shallow convection. Suppressed heating in the dry period is a signature of reduced 0-dBZ ETH occurrence. However, its enhanced occurrence during the wet period resulted heating maxima around 6 km. Near high precipitation events, midtropospheric humidity rapidly builds up over 2±3 days prior to increase in cloud-top heights and areal coverage. Large amplitudes of ETH diurnal cycle during the dry period was accompanied by weak upstream winds and vice versa. Convectively inactive periods had pronounced lightning signatures compared to wet. The lightning occurrences are related with of 30-dBZ top heights above the freezing level and convective area fractions.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of C-band Arletron with Extraction of Microwave Power in TE10-Mode
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this paper, we have performed a simulation study of the light-weighted, compact, and highly efficient arletron in C-band with the novel extraction cavity i.e. rectangular cavity. The electromagnetic behavior of the modulating cavity in the absence of an electron beam and the RF behavior of the modeled device in the presence of an electron beam have been investigated. The model is designed and simulated with the help of CST Microwave studio. The simulation results suggest that the device is able to generate a microwave peak power of the ~500 MW in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>-mode.

articleTitle: FMCW Radars for Volume Scattering from Precipitation
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In weather radars, most of the information about precipitation volume are derived from the received signal. Historically the preferred mode of operation has been pulsed radars, whereas Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars have not been used due to several limitations such as need for two antennas, isolation between transmitter and receiver among other things. However, in the context of low power short range radars this preference must be revisited. FMCW radars can achieve good high resolution as narrow pulse radars but can be done with lower power level due to the CW nature. The radar equation for volume targets in FMCW radar is different from the general pulsed radar. The radar range equation for FMCW weather radars is revisited here to explore the power requirements, for short range urban applications.

articleTitle: Wideband terahertz cross polarization converter based on parallel strip metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: An ultra-wideband terahertz reflective-type cross polarization converter using parallel metallic strips in terahertz domain is demonstrated in this paper. The proposed structure converts a linearly polarized incident wave to cross polarized in the range of frequency extending from 7.86 THz to 15.20 THz. The polarization conversion ratio in the entire operating band is more than 0.85, while the fractional bandwidth is 63.6% corresponding to the center frequency. Furthermore, to check the robustness of the structure, the polarization conversion rate of the structure is examined by varying the incidence angle for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) case. The structure maintains compactness in periodicity (~λ/6.5) as well as ultrathin (~λ/10.5) in nature.

articleTitle: Challenges, Design and Realization of Photoconductive Antennas for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This invited paper aims to provide a brief insight on various challenges and design issues of photoconductive antennas (PCAs) for THz applications. Unlike classical microwave antennas, design and practical realization of PCAs involves not only antenna engineering/antenna physics but also involves input from semiconductor physics, photonics, material science and nano-electronics. This paper presents a broad idea on the working principles of PCAs, steps required for augmenting its performance and discusses various intrinsic challenges associated.

publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this work, the photonics based radar with "4 channel" input and output architecture estimation more precise parameters like as pass through autocorrelation with different -different wavelength LD unit , power estimation with increase cablelength has been investigated thoroughly broad band power-meter and also crosschecked power estimation by using R-SOFT software. A photonics-based 4 ×4 MIMO radar is establish with 3.5 GHz wide bandwidth in photonics based multi-channels signal generation and processing is evaluated and an experiment for 4 channel with WDM techniques of the proposed radar is evaluated. This photonics based MIMO experimental circuit has a potential bandwidth leads to high resolution.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach of Texture Description using DWT and GLCM on Digital Images
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Texture is a predominant characteristic in the images and very useful for identification of the objects. In the present work the focus is on the analysis of textural features in digital images. A dataset containing 8 images has been used in which the size of all images is 640×640 pixels. The Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is used to analyze the texture. Five textural measures, viz., contrast, correlation, energy, and entropy of scaled image are computed on four different offset values 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>, 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>, 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> and 135<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> separately. It is observed that the value of entropy, correlation, energy and homogeneity decrease with the increasing levels of DWT whereas the value of contrast increases with corresponding offset value.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation study for varying Refractive index of a cavity in a Dielectric Whispering Gallery Mode Resonator in THz regime
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The response of varying refractive indices of circular cavity fabricated inside a Whispering Gallery Mode Resonator (WGMR) is modelled and studied using Finite element method. With a view to examine as well as characterize the change caused in the transmittance by the cavity and its corresponding refractive indices, we present simulation results of a rectangular cross-section ring resonator which can be optimized with respect to specific molecules, gases or substances to show a deviant response for various applications.

articleTitle: Study of July 2, 2019 South American Total Solar Eclipse effect on the ionosphere using GPS signal
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In this work, we present the preliminary study of the ionospheric changes during total solar eclipse on July 2 2019 in the south American region. Because of eclipse occurrence timing over the Chilean region, it is a unique event as happened during the local evening time, when ionospheric evolution was going down due to decrease in electron density as intensity of ionizing radiation decreases. Solar eclipse, solar further decreases ionizing radiation. We have chosen two GPS receiving station close to totality path. The SILL station was in totality (magnitude 1.006), while PVCA was in partial (magnitude 0.99) eclipse region. Interestingly, we have observed maximum decrease in electron density (0.56 TEC unit) at PVCA compare to SILL (0.38 TEC unit) station. The higher decrease in electron density at partial eclipse station could possibly due to two regions: local time difference and geographical difference. A more detailed analysis is further warranted to confirm these possibilities.

articleTitle: Storm time PP fields effects and TADs modulations in TEC
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: The latitudinal response to the geomagnetic storm of 15 May 2005 has been examined over the chain of stations extending from the equatorial region to the mid-latitude along the Indian longitude sector. Based upon the TEC observations, it has been settled that the response of the ionosphere to the storm time prompt penetration (PP) fields has latitudinal dependence, although the PP fields infiltrate near-simultaneously from mid to equatorial latitudes. Effect of storm-induced meridional winds on TEC has also been perceived along with modulations in TEC manifested by traveling atmospheric disturbances (TADs).

articleTitle: Scenario of R&D in Microwave Tubes in India vis-à-vis Global Trends
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Historical timeline of microwave tubes (MWTs) dating back to the beginning of the nineteenth century was presented. The competition between MWTs and solid state devices was taken note of. The applications of MWTs were reviewed. MWTs were grouped according to the global trend in R&D in MWTs, and hence Indian efforts following this trend were revisited.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Monopole Antenna with Modified Ground structure
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: this paper proposes a new monopole antenna design comprises of partial modified ground structure (PMGS) with semi-circle ring shaped printed structure featured for circular polarization. At the bottom surface of FR-4 substrate, the partial rectangular ground plane is modified by adjoining two triangular patches at both the corner. Further to achieve the broader axial ratio performance, a small sized rectangular slot positioned just under the feed strip is imprinted from the partial ground plane. Proposed antenna is optimized for optimum performance before fabrication and measured for the validation with simulated results. From the measured results, it is confirmed that the antenna can be competently produced a fractional impedance bandwidth (< -10 dB) nearly $ \approx 26.40\% $ and simulated 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth ≈ 6.65 $\% ,$ respectively. The measured total gain profile is varied from 4.65 dB to 6.78 dB in impedance bandwidth; while the CP gain profile varies from 5.67 dBi to 6.28 dBi with 6.28 dBi peak gain. For the proposed antenna, the cross polar suppression was noticed around $18\;{\text{dB}}$ along with wide 3-dB beamwidth.

articleTitle: Dispersion Control of a Helix Slow-Wave Structure by I-shaped Metamaterial Loading for Wideband Traveling-Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: A simple metamaterial loading scheme for a helical slowwave structure was proposed in lieu of a conventional metal vane loading. The proposed structure consists of a helix in a metal envelope supported by rectangular dielectric rods each with I-shaped metal-strip epsilon-negative metamaterial printed on both of its radial faces. Our study, based on CST simulation, showed that the proposed simple structure gives controlled dispersion as obtained by the conventional vane-loaded helix with large interaction impedance values even higher than those of the latter.

articleTitle: Contaminated effect of Geomagnetic storm on pre-seismic atmospheric and ionospheric anomalies during Imphal earthquake
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: Understanding of Seismo-ionospheric coupling mechanism requires a quiet geomagneticcondition to eliminate any kind of contamination in the lower atmospheric and ionospheric parameters. We present the evidence of such event during a strong earthquake happened in Imphal on January 4, 2016 (M=6.7). We studied the lower ionospheric irregularities using Very Low Frequency radio wave characteristics as observed from fixed frequency transmitter JJI (22.2 kHz) in Japan by using the conventional nighttime fluctuation methods. We also studied the presence of Atmospheric Gravity Wave (AGW) in VLF data and also computed from SABER/TIMED satellite observation. Two geomagnetic storms occurred on December 21, 2015 and January 1, 2016. By the conventional analysis, we found there are significant decrease in nighttime trend and increase in nighttime fluctuations, but seismo-genic effects are quite contaminated due to the storm. The AGW variation shows similar effects but less prominent. By analysis of SABER data, we found enhancement of AGW, but effects are rather post-storm effect instead of pre-seismic. The same results obtained when the presence of wavelike structure are computed from the Fast Fourier Transform of the nighttime VLF data. So, this paper shows a significant example of elimination of contamination of pre-seismic phenomena from other terrestrial solar energetic sources.

articleTitle: Wind Profile Recovery in MST Radar Exploiting the Sparse Signal Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: In atmospheric radars for wind measurements, adequate time domain data is first collected, and then subjected to Fourier domain analysis. This does not explicitly utilize the sparsity of the underlying signal, which is sparse in Doppler domain as well as across altitudes. We therefore propose the acquisition and recovery of atmospheric wind profiles using sparse signal processing techniques. In particular, Compressed Sensing (CS) suggests that a compressible signal can be recovered from a small number of measurements. Incorporating this sparseness, we apply CS recovery techniques such as Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) and Compressive Sampling Matching Pursuit (CoSaMP) to recover the Doppler speeds from a few noisy radar observations. Furthermore, a dynamic program based on Viterbi Data Association (VDA) is employed to reconstruct the wind profile, further exploiting the sparsity across altitudes. We employ a suitable cost metric factoring the kinematics of wind velocities to optimally track the profile. The proposed algorithm is applied on a few offline Indian MST radar datasets, and the performance is compared with that of existing algorithms like Adaptive Moment Estimation (AME) and Multiparameter Cost Function (MPCF). Our experiments prove that sparse signal recovery techniques can identify the true Doppler velocities with improved tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of a High Performance Reflective Linear to Circular Polarization Converter with Wide Axial Ratio Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: This paper presents a high performance reflective linear-to-circular polarization (LCP) converter. The proposed polarization converter consists units of periodically arranged two-dimensional array of diagonally symmetric metallic patterns on top of ultrathin (thickness is 0.036λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is wavelength at mid operating frequency) grounded dielectric substrate. It offers about 30% 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) from 5.84 to 7.91 GHz. The axial ratio response remains quite stable for oblique incidences up to 30° of both TE and TM polarized waves. The polarization states of the reradiated wave are shown by plotting the polarization ellipses at different frequency samples within the ARBW. The proposed LCP converter is fabricated and experimentally measured to validate the numerically simulated results.

articleTitle: Instrumental Calibration for Observations of Redshifted 21-cm Signal from Neutral Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2020 URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science ( URSI-RCRS)
abstract: We investigate the calibration requirements for high dynamic range observations in radio interferometric experiments. Particularly, we access the requirement of the time-dependent instrumental gain calibration for observations of faint diffused emission in the presence of compact and bright diffused sources in the sky. This is particularly important for the observation of the redshifted 21-cm signal from the neutral hydrogen at different stages of the evolution of the universe. Our results suggests an order of magnitude better calibration compared to what is achieved at present is required to estimate the power spectrum of the redshifted 21-cm signal.
